advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=120, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, outer_wall_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB vs iter-1. PRIOR: iter-1 (img_n_bf=1, 6 params) hr=0.0, val_ssim=0.9567, val_psnr=38.44, recon_rmse 9.80e-4 slightly ABOVE baseline_rmse 9.65e-4 (recon marginally WORSE than the clean 128-view FBP -> hr floors at 0). This is the documented N2I-over-smooths-dense-breast failure (findings.md 2026-05-22). KNOB: image-domain BF DEPTH img_n_bf 1->3 (proj_n_bf held at 1). HYPOTHESIS: a deeper image-domain BF cascade (3 stacked TrainableBilateralFilter2d = 12 img params) gives the N2I loss more edge-preserving capacity, so it MIGHT recover fine detail rather than blur -- if hr climbs off 0, depth is a live lever; if it stays 0 (or SSIM/PSNR drop), deeper BF just compounds the over-smoothing and DEPTH is exhausted as an escape from the N2I ceiling. FAILURE MODE watched: over-smoothing (val_psnr drops below iter-1 38.44 / recon_rmse rises above baseline). BUDGET: img_n_bf 1->3 triples image-domain unfold cost but on breast's light 128-view adjoint iter-1 ran 1200s at depth1/n_iter120; depth3 image BF is cheap vs the FBP adjoints, expect <1300s; outer_wall_s=1050 internal backstop unchanged (it cut iter-1 at 195/200 scenes -> val_n effectively ~195, consistent across iters). ONE knob changed: img_n_bf 1->3.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, outer_wall_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=iter-3 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB vs iter-1 (return to img_n_bf=1 baseline; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 was hr=0 SSIM0.9560, marginally WORSE than iter-1 0.9567 -> DEPTH compounds over-smoothing, exhausted). PRIOR: iter-1 (n_iter=120) hr=0 SSIM0.9567 PSNR38.44 recon_rmse 9.80e-4 > baseline 9.65e-4. KNOB: per-scene optimization steps n_iter 120->30 (EARLY-STOP the per-image N2I fit). HYPOTHESIS: the N2I split-MSE target is the noisy 64-view half FBP, so MORE steps pull the recon further BELOW the clean 128-view FBP (over-smooth). With the warm-start init + only 30 per-scene steps the recon stays CLOSER to the raw FBP, so recon_rmse should APPROACH baseline_rmse from above -- if hr ticks off 0, the ceiling is partly a CONVERGENCE artifact and there is an early-stop sweet spot (next: n_iter 10, 60); if hr stays 0, the N2I MSE floor is structural even at the warm-start-dominated regime. FAILURE watched: too few steps -> recon = warm-start-generic-BF (may be WORSE than a good FBP if the generic sigma over-blurs). BUDGET: n_iter 120->30 is ~4x FEWER inner steps -> expect ~350-450s, well under wall (iter-1 depth1/n_iter120 = 1200s). ONE knob: n_iter 120->30.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=2, img_n_bf=1, outer_wall_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=iter-4 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: projection-domain BF DEPTH proj_n_bf 1->2 (vs iter-3 base: proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, n_iter=30). PRIOR trajectory: iter-1 (n_iter120) SSIM0.9567 recon_rmse9.80e-4 > base9.65e-4; iter-2 (img depth3) SSIM0.9560 WORSE; iter-3 (n_iter30 early-stop) SSIM0.9563 recon_rmse9.86e-4 ~= base9.84e-4 (early-stop reaches FBP PARITY but never beats it). All hr=0. So image-domain BF + optimization steps are exhausted; recon asymptotes to FBP from ABOVE. NEW AXIS: the projection (sinogram) domain has only ever been at depth 1. KNOB: proj_n_bf 1->2 (2 stacked projection BFs = extra 3 proj params). HYPOTHESIS: denoising the 64-view half-sinogram MORE before FBP could suppress the sparse-view streak noise that the image-domain BF cannot reach, so the N2I recon might finally dip recon_rmse BELOW baseline (hr>0). If hr stays 0, the projection domain is ALSO bounded by FBP on dense breast and the N2I ceiling is confirmed to hold across BOTH domains. FAILURE watched: findings.md warns projection BF that is too strong -> view inconsistency -> new artifacts (PSNR/SSIM drop). BUDGET: proj depth2 adds one sinogram unfold per half-pass; cheap; n_iter=30 -> ~1000s (iter-3 ran 1047s). ONE knob: proj_n_bf 1->2.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0005, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-5 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: image-domain BF RANGE sigma img_sr 0.02->0.0005 (much tighter intensity bandwidth -> edge-preserving). Back to proj_n_bf=1/img_n_bf=1/n_iter=30 (iter-4 proj depth2 was hr=0 SSIM0.9563 recon_rmse9.85e-4 ~= base9.84e-4 -> projection axis also FBP-bounded). TRAJECTORY so far (all hr=0): depth (img & proj), n_iter/early-stop all asymptote to FBP from above, never below. HYPOTHESIS: the failure is edge-BLINDNESS -- a wide range sigma (0.02) lets the BF average across fibroglandular tissue edges (over-smooth). A TIGHT img_sr=0.0005 (the old-split breast N2I champion value) makes the range kernel edge-preserving: it smooths flat noise but STOPS at intensity edges, so the recon could retain detail AND denoise -> first real shot at recon_rmse < baseline (hr>0). If STILL hr=0, edge-preservation via range sigma does not unlock breast N2I either. FAILURE watched: too-tight img_sr -> BF becomes near-identity (no denoising) -> recon = raw noisy FBP (SSIM/PSNR ~ baseline, not below). BUDGET: img_sr is a VALUE change, same kernel/unfold cost as iter-3 (1047s); outer_wall_s tightened 1050->900 to keep total safely under the 30-min sbatch wall (iter-4 proj-depth2 ran 25 min). ONE knob: img_sr 0.02->0.0005.

HYPOTHESIS: 1 epoch is even less over-smoothed than 2 while still providing the essential non-crash seed -> hr >= 0.2056 (possibly higher if 2 epochs already began mild over-smoothing). ONE knob: pretrain_epochs 2->1.

Breast LD-FBP calibrated baseline_PSNR ~36.3 (baseline is a STRONG sparse-view FBP after calibration); the Mayo-trained wavelet prior (fd_out_scale=0.05) is ~10x mis-normalised vs breast mu~0.5, so at dc_relax=0.5 only HALF the CG-projected (data-consistent) image is blended in and the mis-scaled prior half drags PSNR ~9 dB below baseline -> hr=0. (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_dc_relax 0.5 -> 1.0 (FULL hard-CG DC projection each Euler step; blend the CG-fit image 100%, discard the mis-scaled prior's HU offset). FALSIFIER: if RMSE >= 1.465e-2 (dc_relax INERT or worse), full DC is already saturated at relax0.5 -> iter-3 pivots to fd_recon_init_t lower (0.7->0.4, start reverse-diffusion closer to FBP so the mis-scaled prior has fewer steps to drift HU). (5) BUDGET: dc_relax is FREE (same 8 steps + CG5); iter-1 ran 121s << 1200s budget / 1800s kill. val=ALL 200 seed-20260703 cases. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing via the numeric-RMSE gate.

advice_for_others: itnet-claude-agentic: pretrain_epochs=120, pretrain_lr=0.001, itnet_k=1, itnet_alpha=0.1, unet_c=16, finetune_epochs=0, finetune_lr=0.0001, train_n=400, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=iter-3 (breast ItNet v1, search-20260703-01). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR NUMBERS: iter-1 (k=5, ep=20) ssim 0.8237 hr 0.0000 elapsed 212s; iter-2 (k=5, ep=120) ssim 0.7114 hr 0.0000 elapsed 1184s. CRITICAL SIGNAL: 6x MORE pretraining made ssim DROP 0.8237->0.7114 -> the denoiser is NOT under-trained; MORE denoising quality gets DESTROYED downstream. (2) FAILURE MODE: the FIXED analytic k=5 DC unroll re-injects sparse-view streaks. Mechanism: x <- x_denoised - alpha*FBP(R*x_denoised - g); on a 128-view sparse system FBP(residual) is itself a streaky sparse-view recon, so each of the 5 fixed (untrained) DC steps drags the clean denoised image back toward the streaky FBP, raising RMSE above baseline. A cleaner x_denoised (iter-2) is corrupted MORE by 5 steps -> ssim fell. On Mayo the v1 CHAMPION used k=1 for exactly this reason. (3) ONE KNOB: itnet_k 5 -> 1 (all else identical to iter-2: ep=120, alpha=0.1, unet_c=16, lr=1e-3, train_n=400, val_n=200). (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I cut the fixed DC unroll to a single step (k=1), I expect hr to clear 0 and ssim to jump back above iter-1, because the dominant damage is the repeated streak re-injection; one mild DC step barely perturbs the clean denoiser output. FALSIFIER: if hr is still 0 at k=1, the DC step itself (any alpha>0) is net-harmful on sparse breast -> iter-4 drops alpha toward 0 (or k stays 1 with alpha lowered). (5) BUDGET: k=1 is CHEAPER than k=5 (1 forward+FBP per val slice instead of 5); iter-2 at k=5/ep=120 was 1184s, so k=1/ep=120 predicts well under 1000s < 1200s budget. (6) Loop continues; iter-4 dispatched on landing via numeric-headroom gate.

(5) BUDGET: k=1 is CHEAPER than k=4 at both train (DC in-loop) and val; iter-1 used 240s at k=4, so k=1 is comfortably < 1200s. (6) Loop continues; I dispatch iter-3 myself when iter-2 lands.

SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: none (first iter of slug); nearest ref = Mayo manduca iter-1 hr=0.0598 at these paper-faithful defaults, and the sibling breast DD-UNet-supervised run (same split) clears FBP baseline trivially at hr~0.81. (2) Failure mode: N/A onboarding; goal = does Manduca proj-bilateral run on breast val=200 under 20-min budget and clear the 128-view sparse FBP baseline (hr>0)? (3) ONE KNOB: N/A baseline = paper-faithful CONFIG defaults (proj_n_bf=1, proj_sr=1.5, bf_d_w_ratio=1/6, manduca_N0=1e5=dataset i0, img_n_bf=1, ep=10). (4) HYPOTHESIS: the ~6-9 param Manduca bilateral trains stably on breast (finite val_score, comparison.png) and clears hr>0; but expect a MODEST hr (the noise model targets Poisson photon noise, while breast's dominant defect is 128-view STREAK aliasing, so the proj-bilateral on sqrt-counts is a weak lever here vs the DD-UNet). The image-domain bilateral tail (img_n_bf) is the reserved iter-2+ lever. (5) BUDGET: bilateral is ~6-9 params, far cheaper than the DD-UNet (which ran ep10 train_n=400 val=200 in 227s); ep10 fits well under 20 min (30-min sbatch wall). breast uses a single shared PYRO-NN projector (no per-sample-ps swap), FBP batched, val_chunk=10 fine. Reserved knobs for iters 2-N: img_n_bf (image-domain denoise depth, the primary lever mirroring Mayo bilateral-supervised), proj_sr, bf_d_w_ratio, epochs.

FALSIFIER: if hr stays <=~0.22, image-domain depth is not the lever -> iter-3 attacks the proj-domain (proj_sr / bf_d_w_ratio) or epochs. (5) BUDGET: +2 cheap bilateral passes/step; iter-1 ran 107s so this stays far under the 20-min budget (30-min sbatch wall). (6) Loop continues; iter-3 dispatched on landing. --qos=turbo active.

advice_for_others: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=20, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=128, naf_layers=4, naf_n_iter=5000, naf_lr=0.01, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1000, naf_per_scene_s=48.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 FEASIBILITY (breast-ct-claude-agentic-naf-search-20260703-01, REDONE breast split train3600/val200/test200 seed20260703). GOAL: does naf (Neural Attenuation Field, per-scene self-supervised INR -- one coordinate-MLP optimized PER breast slice against its OWN 128-view sinogram, no training set) run on the redone breast_ct staged val split and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png + recon_raw.npz WITHIN the HARD 20-min budget, scoring under the frozen calibrated-headroom metric (display 0..0.05, mu>=0 floor, FOV-masked)? BUDGET REASONING (load-bearing): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. Per the user hint, naf is HEAVY so I use a SMALL val_n=20 (NOT 200) kept CONSTANT across all 20 iters so they are comparable (breast val load is deterministic first-20 of the 200-case val split). 1000s outer wall / 20 scenes = 48 s/scene (naf_per_scene_s=48), inside the 20-min compute budget with figure+IO headroom before the 30-min sbatch kill. breast is 512x512 at 128 views x det; each Adam step = a 512^2 MLP forward + 128-view fan-beam forward-project + backward. 48 s/scene buys HUNDREDS of steps -- a GENUINE NeRF-style per-scene fit, so hr=0 here would be a STRUCTURAL verdict, NOT budget starvation. naf_n_iter=5000 is a HIGH CAP so the PER-SCENE WALL (t_limit in fit_one_scene), NOT the iter count, is the governor. Leaner MLP than default (hidden 192->128, layers 5->4, n_freqs 10->8) for cheaper steps => more steps/scene; naf_lr 5e-3->1e-2 converges faster from the water-mu init in a bounded budget. naf_n_clip=0.05 (sigmoid head out_scale), naf_tv_weight=1e-4 defaults. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense-view (128-angle) breast-CT -- docs/findings.md 2026-05-23 confirms NAF's sin/cos-posenc coordinate-MLP basis is too coarse for dense soft-tissue at 512^2/128-views and cannot beat the ~0.84 breast LD-FBP baseline (hr=0) even at 5x n_iter. Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the FBP baseline (hr near 0). This iter ESTABLISHES that datapoint on the redone split under the frozen metric -- a real, valid finding (do NOT reduce val_n further or inflate to make NAF look better; hr=0 plateau documents the ceiling for paper section 5.4).

SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: none (first iter this slug); documented ceiling (docs/findings.md 2026-06-03): R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY bounded on dense 128-view breast -> hr=0 confirmed at gs_n_iter 300->40k and with FBP warm-start; the anisotropic-Gaussian basis is too coarse for densely-distributed soft tissue at 512^2/128-view, and the 128-view FBP baseline is already very strong (SSIM ~0.957). (2) FAILURE MODE: N/A onboarding; goal = does r2gaussian run on the new breast val=15 split under the HARD 20-min budget, and does it clear the 128-view sparse-FBP baseline (hr>0)? Expect hr=0 per the documented ceiling. (3) ONE KNOB: N/A baseline (mirrors the Mayo iter-1 knobs adapted to breast: 512 Gaussians / 150 steps / default LRs). (4) HYPOTHESIS: cold-init 512-Gaussian / 150-step per-scene fit lands BELOW the 128-view FBP baseline on RMSE -> hr=0, because the Gaussian basis is too sparse for dense breast soft tissue (findings 2026-06-03). If hr>0, the ceiling is refuted and I re-map; if hr=0 at SSIM ~0.88-0.94 (per prior breast R2-G), the documented ceiling reproduces on the new split. (5) BUDGET: 15 scenes x ~41 s = ~615 s + FBP-load + scoring + figure << 1200 s HARD < 1800 s (30-min) SLURM wall; gs_outer_wall_s=1080 self-truncates before the SLURM kill. (6) STRICT SERIAL, one job at a time; loop continues, iter-2 self-dispatched on the per-JOBID DONE sentinel. Reserved levers for iters 2-N: gs_n_iter, gs_n_gaussians, gs_init_from_fbp, gs_ssim_weight, gs_lr_*.

RE-DISPATCH REASON: the first iter-2 attempt (gs_n_iter=250, NO gs_outer_wall_s in cfg) fell back to the solver-default 600s in-solver wall and TRUNCATED at sample 10/15 on the RTX 5000 node (~66 s/scene) -> val_n dropped to 10, breaking the val_n=15-CONSTANT requirement (it still gave hr=0, SSIM 0.8033, PSNR 20.32 on the 10 completed). FIX: add gs_outer_wall_s=1080 (generous, never fires for 15 scenes) AND reduce steps 250->220 so all 15 scenes finish on the slower shared nodes: 220 steps x ~58 s/scene x 15 = ~870 s < 1080 wall < 1200 s HARD < 1800 s SLURM. PRIOR NUMBERS: iter-1 hr=0.0000, SSIM=0.8032, PSNR=20.14, RMSE=0.03231, 15/15 scenes, vs 128-view FBP baseline PSNR=35.97 (hr=0). FAILURE MODE: per-scene 512-Gaussian recon lands FAR below the strong sparse-FBP baseline (basis too coarse for dense breast soft tissue / possible under-fit). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.80 flat, 150-220 steps already saturate the Gaussian basis -> quality is NOT the lever (basis-coarseness ceiling). hr expected 0 either way (matching FBP PSNR 35.9 with 512 Gaussians in 220 steps is implausible). val_n=15 HELD CONSTANT (now enforced by gs_outer_wall_s=1080). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 SSIM 0.8032 @150 steps -> iter-2 @220 steps quality test., gs_outer_wall_s=1080

FAILURE MODE: the coarse anisotropic-Gaussian basis cannot reconstruct dense breast soft tissue near the strong sparse-FBP baseline; warm-start gave the biggest lift (it literally seeds from FBP) yet stays far below the FBP floor on the PSNR/RMSE-gated headroom. BUDGET: SSIM term = 1 cheap conv/step vs the dominating projection -> same ~990s as iter-4 << 1080 wall. TRAJECTORY: iter-4 0.8539 (warm-start, BEST) -> iter-5 SSIM-loss @0.15 test., gs_outer_wall_s=1080, gs_amp_init_max=0.05

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.0001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-2 (breast_ct). DIAGNOSIS of iter-1 (step_init=1e-2): hr=0.0, val_psnr=17.27 dB -- 19 dB WORSE than the LD-FBP baseline (36.32 dB), val_ssim 0.719 vs baseline 0.920. SLURM training log (job 772163) is the smoking gun: loss FROZEN at 0.004813 across ALL 10 epochs and every learned step[k]=0.01 / lambda[k]=0.001 PINNED at init (only step_9 drifted to 0.00937). FAILURE MODE (named): STEP-TOO-LARGE OVERSHOOT -> saturated-gradient training freeze. Mechanism (docs/findings.md 2026-05-23 + Mayo iter-3): the data gradient R^T(R f - g) uses the RAW unnormalized adjoint of the 128-view breast forward op; tv_step_init=0.01 (inherited from the classical sibling's tv_lr) is ~operator-norm too large, so f - 0.01*R^T(...) overshoots into a bad clamped basin at K=1, the clamp/divergence kills the gradient to the 20 log-scalars -> they never move -> recon diverges from FBP regardless of epochs. baseline FBP PSNR=36.32 confirms data/projector are fine; only the unrolled step scale is wrong. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-2 -> 1e-4 (100x smaller; keeps the unrolled iteration INSIDE the stable basin near FBP where gradients flow to the scalars). Historical breast iter-2 (findings 2026-05-23) used exactly step_init=1e-4 and the recon stayed near FBP (loss dropped, scalars departed init). All else IDENTICAL to iter-1 (K=10, train_n=400, epochs=10, bs=1, lambda_init=1e-3, lr=5e-3, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: at 100x smaller step the training UN-FREEZES -- loss DECREASES across epochs, step[k]/lambda[k] DEPART from init, and val_psnr recovers from 17.3 toward/above the FBP floor (36.3 dB) so hr rises above 0. FALSIFIER: if loss stays flat AND scalars stay pinned, the harness is deeper-broken (then iter-3 attacks init: drop FBP-init / zero-init, or deepen K). BUDGET: iter-1 ran 750s total (<1200s wall); identical compute -> ~750s.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-3 (breast_ct). BRACKET the step regime. iter-1 (step=1e-2): OVERSHOOT -> diverged 19 dB below FBP, hr=0. iter-2 (step=1e-4): training un-froze BUT the optimiser drove step[k] DOWN to ~6e-7 (a near-no-op), so the recon converged to EXACTLY the LD-FBP init (val_psnr 36.31 vs baseline 36.32, ssim 0.9198 vs 0.9199) -> hr=0. NAMED failure mode: FBP-INIT ZERO-GRADIENT TRAP (findings 2026-05-23) -- since R+ ~= FBP, the data-gradient R^T(R*FBP - g) ~= 0 at init, so the supervised loss's only signal is stay-put; too-small a step lets it sit on FBP, too-large a step diverges. The productive regime is BETWEEN 1e-4 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-4 -> 1e-3 (geometric midpoint of the bracket; 10x iter-2, 10x below the iter-1 overshoot). All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (K=10, train_n=400, epochs=10, bs=1, lambda_init=1e-3, lr=5e-3, val_n=200). HYPOTHESIS: at step=1e-3 the unrolled TV iteration is large enough to move the recon OFF the FBP fixed point and do real denoising work, yet small enough to stay in the stable basin (no divergence), so val_psnr rises ABOVE the FBP floor (>36.3 dB) and hr clears 0. FALSIFIER: if step=1e-3 also diverges (like 1e-2) the stable band is narrow -> iter-4 bisects toward 3e-4; if it again collapses to FBP (step driven to ~0) the FBP fixed point is a strong attractor for the data term at ANY stable step -> iter-4 attacks it via tv_lambda_init UP (stronger TV prior gradient to pull off FBP). BUDGET: iter-2 ran ~750s (<1200s wall); identical compute.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=50, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (breast_ct). DEPTH probe. iter-1/2/3 mapped the step axis: 1e-2 diverges (hr0), 1e-4 and 1e-3 both COLLAPSE the learned step to ~0 so the K=10 recon sits on the FBP init (psnr~36.3=baseline, hr0). NAMED failure: at K=10 the optimiser prefers step->0 because FBP-init already has MSE-optimal psnr 36.3 and 10 TV steps cannot out-denoise it, so staying put minimises the supervised MSE. KEY CONTRAST: the classical (non-learned) tv_iterative sibling BEATS FBP on this exact split (hr 0.16 at 200 iters -> 0.355 at 1000 iters) using the SAME TV iteration but with MANY iterations at fixed non-zero step/lambda -- it does real iterative denoising that K=10 cannot reach. HYPOTHESIS: the limiter is UNROLL DEPTH, not step scale -- with enough steps the TV iteration can denoise the FBP noise below FBP's own MSE, giving the optimiser a reason to KEEP step non-zero. ONE KNOB: tv_K 10 -> 50 (5x depth; step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3 kept from iter-3). All else identical. EXPECT: step[k] no longer collapses to 0, recon departs FBP with net denoising, val_psnr rises above 36.3 and hr clears 0. FALSIFIER: if step still collapses to 0 and hr stays 0, depth is NOT the limiter and the FBP fixed point is a hard supervised-MSE attractor at any K (matches findings 2026-05-23 verdict) -> iter-5 switches loss (l1) or attacks lambda. BUDGET: iter-3 ran ~750s at K=10; K=50 is 5x the unrolled fwd/bwd in BOTH train and val. Train ~5x, val ~5x -> est ~ (750-load)*~3 + load. Conservatively ~900-1100s; still under the 1200s wall. If it risks the wall iter-5 trims val_n or epochs.

advice_for_others: wu_2015-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=6, wu_n_outer=0, wu_motion_range=8, wu_motion_window=2, wu_soft_thresh=0.0015, val_n=200, val_chunk=4, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (one knob vs iter-1). NUMBERS: iter-1 hr=0.0 (n_outer=2): Wu recon val_ssim=0.469 PSNR=22.80 RMSE=0.0247, but the plain FBP baseline is ssim=0.920 PSNR=36.32 RMSE=0.00521 -> Wu RMSE is 4.7x WORSE than baseline, hr=0. FAILURE MODE: the residual-refinement OUTER LOOP (forward-project the aliasing-free FBP, subtract, feature-preserving-interp the residual to 2x angles, FBP + soft-threshold + add-back) is INJECTING artefacts, not recovering aliasing structure -- on dense 128-view breast data the view-aliasing is mild so the densified residual is mostly error. ONE KNOB: wu_n_outer 2 -> 0 (skips the entire outer loop; returns the pure aliasing-free band-split FBP alone, 0 params). All else = iter-1. HYPOTHESIS: if I remove the residual add-back loop I expect val hr to rise above 0 (RMSE to drop toward/below the 0.00521 baseline) because the band-split aliasing-free FBP alone avoids the mis-estimated residual densification; if the band-split FBP alone still trails plain-FBP baseline, the band-splitting itself (not just the residual loop) is the problem and iter-3 sweeps n_bands. Budget: ~4s recon, trivially <20min.

advice_for_others: wu_2015-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=1, wu_n_outer=0, wu_motion_range=8, wu_motion_window=2, wu_soft_thresh=0.0015, val_n=200, val_chunk=4, seed=42, rationale=ITER-3 (one knob vs iter-2). NUMBERS: iter-1 hr=0 (n_bands=6,n_outer=2: RMSE=0.0247); iter-2 hr=0 (n_bands=6,n_outer=0: RMSE=0.401 PSNR=-1.4 -- pure band-split FBP is CATASTROPHICALLY under-scaled). DIAGNOSIS: aliasing_free_fbp normalises the per-band radial sigmoid weights to sum=1 across bands (weights/wsum), but the band filters PARTITION the ramp |f| (they sum to |f|). Weight-summing the band back-projections with weights that sum to 1 AVERAGES them instead of SUMMING -> the recon is scaled down ~1/n_bands at fully-supported inner pixels. The n_outer=2 residual add-back in iter-1 partially rescaled it (RMSE 0.401->0.0247) but never reached the 0.00521 FBP baseline. ONE KNOB: wu_n_bands 6 -> 1 (n_outer stays 0). At n_bands=1 there is a single band, wsum normalisation gives weight=1 everywhere and the single band filter = the FULL |f| ramp, so aliasing_free_fbp degenerates to a plain ramp FBP. HYPOTHESIS: if n_bands=1 gives RMSE ~= the 0.00521 FBP baseline (hr near 0 but val_ssim ~0.92, PSNR ~36) it CONFIRMS the multi-band weight-normalisation mis-scaling is the whole story (the classical Wu band-split is structurally lossy vs baseline on dense 128-view breast data); if instead single-band clears baseline, that is the operating point to refine. Budget: ~4s.

Risk: too heavy a thresh also removes genuine residual detail (RMSE back up) -> then optimum thresh is in (0.0015,0.003) and I bisect. Budget: ~seconds.

The lever here is to push HIGHER, not just clear baseline. Design-doc hint (solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md 'Hints for the next autoresearch agent'): the projection-domain stack is in the symmetry trap on phantoms (proj sigmas near-identity -> stacked proj BFs stay locked-symmetric, proj_n_bf increase = wasted params), so spend the parameter budget on the IMAGE side. The image-domain stack 'readily differentiates into a multi-scale cascade (BF1 mild + tight sigma_r, BF2 wider, BF3 widest)'. img_n_bf 1->3 grows the image denoiser from 3 to 9 trainable scalars (total network 6->12 params, still ultra-low) for a genuine multi-scale image-domain cascade. Held fixed: proj_n_bf=1 (no point stacking the near-identity proj filter), kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), all six sigma inits (proj 1.0/2.0/0.02, img 1.5/1.5/0.02), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1). Wall: iter-1 ran 126 s; adding 2 image-domain BFs per FBP roughly 2-3x the per-step image cost but image-domain is a tiny fraction of the 128-view FBP+proj cost, so well under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard. Hypothesis: a 3-deep image-domain bilateral cascade gives the denoiser multi-scale capacity (coarse smoothing + edge-preserving fine pass) that a single image BF cannot, lifting val_score above iter-1's 0.6657 without the proj-stack symmetry waste -- and without enough parameters to memorise (12 scalars). If it does NOT move val_score, that confirms the image-domain BF is also near its structural ceiling on this dense phantom substrate and the next iter should pivot to img kernel/sigma tuning instead of depth.

UNDOING THE iter-4 REGRESSION. Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 val 0.6657/hr+0.2763/PSNR 19.47; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 val 0.7465/hr+0.3276/PSNR 20.10; iter-3 img_n_bf=5 val 0.7705/hr+0.3335/PSNR 20.18 (HR-BEST); iter-4 tightened img_sr 0.02->0.0005 -> SSIM ticked up to 0.7709 but hr COLLAPSED 0.3335->0.1998 and PSNR fell 20.18->18.60. Failure mode: tight img_sr is the WRONG lever for demo's substrate. The mayo_campaign_state.md 'tighten img_sr->0.0005 for edge preservation' insight is BREAST-specific (tight=good on dense fibroglandular breast); on demo's sparse ellipse phantoms the tight range sigma OVER-SHARPENS - it forces the 5-deep image cascade to act only across hard intensity jumps and stop smoothing the broad noise floor, so noise/PSNR worsens (20.18->18.60 dB) even though the SSIM structural term inches up. headroom is the campaign's primary structurally-bounded score and it is PSNR/noise-sensitive here, so the over-sharpen is net-negative. The img_sr lever is SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC and OPPOSITE between breast (tight=good) and demo (loose=good). Reverting img_sr 0.0005->0.02 restores the iter-3 hr-0.3335 regime, where the loose range sigma lets the deep cascade do its proven coarse-to-fine NOISE smoothing (the demo lever that earned hr 0.276->0.328->0.335 via img_n_bf 1->3->5 at img_sr=0.02). Chose the clean SINGLE-numeric-knob revert (img_sr only) over also pushing img_n_bf 5->7 in the same iter, to first cleanly RECOVER hr 0.3335 and re-confirm the loose-img_sr regime before iter-6 pushes the proven depth lever further. Held fixed at the iter-3/iter-4 values: img_n_bf=5, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3/4). Wall: iter-4 ran 264 s; img_sr is an init value, zero added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s guard. Hypothesis: reverting the image-domain range sigma to the looser 0.02 undoes the iter-4 over-sharpen and recovers val_score/hr to ~iter-3 (SSIM ~0.7705, hr ~0.3335, PSNR ~20.18), confirming that on demo's substrate loose img_sr is correct (opposite to breast). Trajectory by HEADROOM: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 hr 0.2763 (PSNR 19.47); iter-2 img_n_bf=3 hr 0.3276 (PSNR 20.10, +0.051); iter-3 img_n_bf=5 hr 0.3335 (PSNR 20.18, +0.007 HR-BEST); iter-4 img_sr->0.0005 hr 0.1998 REGRESSED (wrong-direction range-sigma lever, over-sharpen, PSNR 18.60); iter-5 img_sr->0.02 revert hr 0.3320 RECOVERED to ~iter-3. The img_sr range-sigma lever is EXHAUSTED and substrate-confirmed: demo wants LOOSE img_sr=0.02 (opposite to breast), tightening HURTS hr. The proj-domain stack is in the symmetry trap (proj sigmas near-identity per the design doc -> proj_n_bf stays 1, wasted params). That leaves image-domain DEPTH (img_n_bf) as the only proven hr lever on demo, the same lever that earned the whole arc hr 0.276->0.328->0.335. PROBE/HYPOTHESIS: push the proven depth lever one notch further, 5->7, growing the image denoiser from 15 to 21 trainable scalars (total network 16->22 params, still ultra-low, far too few to memorise 6 val scenes). Two more BFs add two coarse-to-fine scales to the multi-scale cascade for additional noise-floor smoothing -- the demo-relevant axis since hr here is PSNR/noise-sensitive. This DOUBLES as the ceiling-doc probe: depth gains are sharply diminishing (1->3 gave +0.051 hr, 3->5 gave only +0.007 hr, PSNR flat 20.10->20.18), so expect <=+0.003 hr. If hr flattens (or regresses), it CONFIRMS demo bilateral N2I is at its structural ceiling (~hr 0.33) -- the 21-scalar image cascade cannot extract more than the half-view FBP noise floor allows on this 128-view synthetic phantom substrate -- and the next iter should stop chasing depth and instead document the ceiling (seed/n_iter/pretrain_epochs invariance probe) rather than tune another smoothing knob. Chose img_n_bf 5->7 over (a) img_sr (exhausted, wrong-direction, hr 0.3335->0.1998), (b) proj_n_bf (symmetry trap, wasted params), (c) img_kernel/img_sx/img_sy (less-informed guesses with no headroom evidence) -- depth is the ONLY lever with a demonstrated positive hr slope on demo. Held fixed at iter-3/iter-5 values: img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3/4/5). Wall: iter-5 ran 249 s; two more image-domain BFs add only a small fraction of the 128-view FBP+proj per-step cost, so comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (well under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=800, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-7: ONE knob changed vs iter-6 (n_iter 400->800, the per-scan Adam fit budget); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_06.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct). CEILING-DOC PROBE, not another smoothing knob. Trajectory by HEADROOM (the campaign primary metric, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-1 img_n_bf=1 hr 0.2763 (PSNR 19.47); iter-2 n_bf=3 hr 0.3276 (+0.051); iter-3 n_bf=5 hr 0.3335 (+0.006, depth HR-BEST); iter-4 img_sr->0.0005 hr 0.1998 REGRESSED; iter-5 img_sr->0.02 revert hr 0.3320 recovered; iter-6 n_bf=7 hr 0.3330 (+0.000 vs n_bf=5, SSIM +0.009 0.7705->0.7796 but hr DEAD FLAT). FAILURE MODE: the image-domain DEPTH lever (img_n_bf) has hit its HEADROOM ceiling -- depth still lifts the SSIM structural term but its hr slope collapsed to zero by n_bf=5 (slope +0.051 -> +0.006 -> 0.000). img_sr is exhausted and substrate-confirmed wrong-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening collapses hr). proj_n_bf is in the symmetry trap (near-identity proj sigmas -> wasted params). So all the SMOOTHING/CAPACITY axes are exhausted on hr. The remaining open question for the ceiling claim is OPTIMIZATION budget: is hr ~0.333 the half-view FBP noise-floor bound (structural), or is the per-scan Adam fit simply stopping short at n_iter=400? Per the per-image N2I knob insights (mayo_campaign_state.md): U-Net N2I OVERFITS each scan as n_iter rises (no early-stop -> demo-n2i 0.4785->0.4293 @n_iter1200), but the 6-param BILATERAL physically CANNOT overfit one scan -- so doubling its per-scan budget is the clean diagnostic the U-Net could not give: more steps either (a) lift hr -> the plateau was under-optimization, the lever is n_iter (and lr), not depth; or (b) leave hr flat at ~0.333 -> CONFIRMS the structural half-view FBP ceiling, after which iter-8+ should stop tuning and document the ceiling with a seed/pretrain_epochs invariance probe toward iter-20. Chose n_iter over (a) img_n_bf 7->9 (depth lever's hr slope is already zero -- a 4th depth step re-confirms iter-6 with near-zero EV on hr), (b) lr (would confound the budget question -- vary n_iter first at the proven lr=2.3e-3, then lr if n_iter moves hr), (c) img_kernel/img_sx/img_sy (less-informed smoothing guesses, no hr evidence). Held fixed at iter-6 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1..6). Wall: iter-6 ran ~260 s; doubling the per-scan fit roughly doubles the per-image loop to ~450-520 s, still well under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). Hypothesis: hr stays ~0.333 even at n_iter=800 -- the 6-param bilateral cannot overfit and has already converged on the half-view FBP noise floor, so more fit budget yields no hr -> CONFIRMS demo bilateral N2I is at its structural ~hr 0.33 ceiling toward iter-20. If instead hr rises meaningfully (>+0.005), the plateau was optimizer-budget-limited and n_iter (then lr) becomes the live lever. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-3: ONE knob -> per-scan lr 1e-3 -> 1e-4 (10x lower). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the plateau is NOT under-convergence. iter-1 (n_iter=400) PSNR 16.13/SSIM 0.4785; iter-2 (n_iter=1200, 3x steps) PSNR 15.99/SSIM 0.4293 -> tripling per-scan steps made it STRICTLY WORSE. A fit approaching its FBP-bounded optimum would rise or plateau; it DEGRADES, the signature of the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITTING each single noisy scan's split-view N2I objective. The per-image loop has no early-stop/best-iter pick (solver _fit_one_scene takes the FINAL predict after a fixed n_iter), so extra Adam steps at lr=1e-3 walk the recon away from the decent warm-start init toward a noise-fitting minimum BELOW the 16.67 dB LD-FBP baseline (hr=0). FAILURE MODE = per-image overfitting of an over-parameterized denoiser to one noisy scan. PROOF the warm-start+per-image plumbing is fine: the BILATERAL twin (identical pipeline, identical warm_start/n_iter=400/seed=42 -> SAME 6 val scenes) hit PSNR 19.47/SSIM 0.6657 hr+0.2763 at its iter-1 and climbed to 0.7465 -- its 6-12-param BF physically CANNOT overfit a single scan, which is exactly why it clears baseline while the U-Net dives under. So the lever is NOT n_iter (saturated/counterproductive) and NOT unet_c (the solver design doc explicitly warns 'don't waste iters on U-Net width: capacity is not the lever for this loss on this dataset'; the BF gained from capacity because BF capacity is structurally constrained, the U-Net's is not). The lever is the per-scan STEP SIZE: drop lr 10x to 1e-4 so Adam stays anchored near the warm-start init (the good operating point the BF twin proves exists) instead of descending into the single-scan noise-fitting minimum. n_iter trimmed 1200 -> 600 (less overshoot needed at low lr; keeps wall short). HYPOTHESIS: at lr=1e-4 the per-image fit barely moves off warm-start, so SSIM/PSNR rise toward and above the 16.67 dB LD-FBP baseline (target: break the 0.4785 plateau, ideally approach the BF twin's ~0.66 / the historical demo_dl N2I hr 0.3811); if SSIM is still flat at ~0.47 the warm-start init itself is the floor and iter-4 should toggle warm_start / raise pretrain_epochs. WALL: warm 3x200=600 + per-image 6x600=3600 = 4200 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 350 s (iter-1 was 250s at 3000 steps), well under the 15-min target, the outer_wall_s=1200 guard, and the 1800 s sbatch wall. All other knobs IDENTICAL to iter-2 (train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, unet_c=16).

DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-1 lr1e-3/n_iter400 SSIM 0.4785; iter-2 n_iter1200 0.4293 (more per-scan steps HURT -> per-image overfit, n_iter ruled out); iter-3 lr1e-3->1e-4 0.4880 (+0.01, the overfit-anchor lever). SSIM rose only 0.4785->0.4880, i.e. essentially the warm-start floor. FIRST ceiling-RAISER attempt since iter-5 (0.50811 hr0, the run best); iters 6-16 never beat it (iters 13-16 were val_n=24 noise-floor reads: seed42=0.4616 / seed123=0.4431 / seed7=0.4257 / seed2024=0.4379, 4-seed mean 0.4421 std 0.0143, hr 0 throughout). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-16 (seed7->2024) SSIM 0.43794 PSNR 13.95 hr0; best ever = iter-5 0.50811 (seed42/ep12/lr1e-4/val_n6). FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan in the no-early-stop _fit_one_scene loop (the 6-param bilateral twin physically CANNOT overfit, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr~0 at 0.43-0.51 SSIM); the per-image fit is FBP-bounded AND has a large init-driven stochastic noise floor (now well-documented). EXHAUSTED / FORBIDDEN recon axes (do NOT retry, per handoff): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293, per-scan overfit), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.0595, load-bearing-positive), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 bracket 1e-4 as the per-scan optimum), unet_c (design-doc warned-against; mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508). val_n is a noise-floor-READ axis (6->12->24), not a recon lever. LEVER CHOICE (the one genuinely-untried ALLOWED knob value): grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.3. grad_clip is applied as clip_grad_norm_(params, gc) in BOTH the warm-start pre-pass (solver lines 263-264) and the per-scan Adam loop (lines 137-138). LOWERING it tightens the per-step gradient-norm cap, which ANCHORS each per-scan fit more tightly near the good warm-start init across all 600 steps -- directly attacking the named per-scan-overfitting failure mode. Lowering can NEVER trigger the 2304/128-view FBP-adjoint overflow the guard exists to prevent (it only REDUCES gradient magnitude), so it is both SAFE and on-mandate; prior iters deliberately declined RAISING grad_clip, but LOWERING it has never been tried. Reset to the seed42 PEAK basin (the good basin, not the iter-16 seed2024 basin) so the grad_clip contrast is clean against the iter-13 seed42/val_n24 read (0.4616). HYPOTHESIS: if per-scan U-Net overfitting (not the FBP bound) is what holds SSIM below the iter-5 0.508 peak, the tighter clip keeps Adam pinned near the warm-start init, lifting the val_n=24 seed42 mean above the iter-13 0.4616 read toward/past iter-5 0.508 -- and possibly nudging hr off 0. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays in the 0.43-0.47 band the floor is the FBP bound itself (not optimization), FINALIZING the structural ceiling for the iter-20 writeup. hr expected ~0 either way (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). WALL: step budget UNCHANGED vs iter-13/14/15/16 (warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 24x600=14400 = 16800 steps); those ran 1400-1651 s. grad_clip changes neither step count nor per-step cost, so wall is identical, under the outer_wall_s=1700 guard and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. All recon-affecting knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-13 seed42/val_n24 config (train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1700); ONLY grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.3 changed.

ONE KNOB: recon_eta 30.0->1.0 (DPS guidance gain). iter-1 (eta=30) = SSIM 0.3937 / hr 0.0 / PSNR 14.31 / RMSE 0.00963 — FAR BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor, i.e. the recon is corrupted relative to its own FBP init, not merely prior-dominated drift. Failure mode: the DPS step is adaptively normalized in-solver (step = (eta/||resid||)*grad, Chung 2023 eq.12), so eta is a dimensionless gain whose literature/demo/breast default is 1.0; eta=30 (a discarded-614 boundary-metric hint) is a 30x overshoot that, with recon_eta_clamp=false (no per-step displacement cap), blows the FBP-initialized iterate off-manifold every reverse step, and the relax=1.0 hard-DC then re-noises a corrupted x0. HYPOTHESIS: lowering eta 30->1 lets the DPS correction be a gentle pull, recovering SSIM from 0.39 toward/above the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.39-0.5 (still <<FBP) at eta=1, the DPS step size was NOT the issue — the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is mismatched to rebinned Mayo under the 25-step low-T budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful under DPS/DC) -> iter-3 redirects to the prior, not the DC weight. BUDGET: eta is free (no per-slice cost change); iter-1 ran 214 slices in 1018.96 s = 4.76 s/slice = 17.0 min < 20-min wall (1800s in-solver backstop never hit). val=ALL 214 L277, 321px geometry FOV default.

ONE KNOB: recon_dcstep_relax 1.0->0.3 (the constrained-specific hard-CG blend; eta held at iter-2's 1.0). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 eta=30 SSIM 0.3937/hr0; iter-2 eta 30->1 REGRESSED to SSIM 0.2366/hr0 -> eta is the WRONG lever (gentling the DPS gain did not help; the corruption is elsewhere). FAILURE MODE (numbers): both prior iters ran recon_dcstep_relax=1.0 = FULL hard projection. In dc_step_cg() the return is relax*x_cg + (1-relax)*x0_mu; relax=1.0 discards the diffusion x0 estimate ENTIRELY and substitutes n_cg=3 Gauss-Newton least-squares fit to the NOISY 2304-view LD sinogram, which is then re-noised back to t_next every 5 reverse steps (warmup 5). That least-squares fit overfits measurement noise and overwrites the prior's structure -> hard-CG DC re-noises a corrupted x0, exactly the constrained variant's failure. The SOLVER DEFAULT is relax=0.5; relax=1.0 was an untested aggressive choice carried from iter-1. ONE KNOB: relax 1.0->0.3 blends 30% CG-projected + 70% diffusion x0, a GENTLE pull to data consistency that preserves prior structure instead of overwriting it. HYPOTHESIS: softening the hard-DC blend lifts SSIM back toward / above the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (hr>0); predicted iter-3 SSIM 0.4-0.7 range (recovery from 0.2366). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays well below FBP (~0.3 vs 0.81) even at relax=0.3, the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is STRUCTURALLY MISMATCHED to rebinned Mayo under the 25-step low-T DPS/DC budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful) -> NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP diffusion on Mayo. BUDGET: relax is a blend scalar inside dc_step_cg -> ZERO compute change (same n_cg=3, n_steps=25, DC cadence every5). iter-2 ran ALL 214 L277 slices in 1033.8 s = 4.83 s/slice = 17.2 min < 20-min wall (1800s in-solver backstop never hit); iter-1 1018.96 s. iter-3 lands ~17 min, inside budget. val=ALL 214 L277, 321px detector-geometry FOV default.

advice_for_others: diffusion_recon_dcstep_constrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=28, recon_eta=30.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-4 search-20260619-01 CONSTRAINED diff-recon — CONFIRMATION iter (last untried lever). BASE = iter-1 BEST config (eta=30.0, relax=1.0, every5/n_cg3/warmup5), NOT iter-2/3: the eta+relax levers are EXHAUSTED and both REGRESSED from iter-1. TRAJECTORY (val=ALL 214 L277, 321px geometry FOV): iter-1 eta=30/relax=1.0/T=25 SSIM 0.3937 (BEST) / hr 0; iter-2 eta 30->1 -> 0.2366 (regressed); iter-3 relax 1.0->0.3 -> 0.2377 (flat). All hr 0, all stuck in the 0.24-0.39 band, FAR below the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor. ONE KNOB: recon_sample_steps 25->28 (the DDIM reverse-step count T = the last untried lever, restarted from the iter-1 best config). FAILURE MODE (numbers): the recon sits 0.39 vs the 0.81 FBP floor and eta (DPS gain) + relax (hard-DC blend) both FAILED to move it off that band -> the corruption is NOT a step-size or DC-weight issue; the remaining hypothesis is that the 25-step low-T DDIM schedule is too coarse to let the constrained hard-DC trajectory converge. The unconstrained sibling's n_steps lever was ALSO flat (T 25->32: 0.396->0.387, hr 0), which is the strong prior that T-up won't help on the constrained side either. HYPOTHESIS: if a finer 28-step schedule meaningfully helped, SSIM would clear the ~0.81 FBP floor (hr>0); I predict it stays ~0.3-0.4 / hr 0 (cf. unconstrained T-up flat). FALSIFIER: if SSIM clears the FBP floor (hr>0) -> the Mayo v4 prior is NOT structurally mismatched, just T-budget-limited -> keep climbing T. If SSIM stays ~0.3-0.4 / hr 0 -> the eta, relax, AND T levers are all exhausted: FILE THE DIFFUSION-PRIOR-MISMATCH VERDICT (Mayo v4 DDPM globally faithful but not conditionally faithful under DPS/DC, mirroring the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict); the constrained best stays iter-1 (SSIM 0.394, hr 0). BUDGET: cost is linear in n_steps (sample_guided loops `for k in range(n_steps)`, one UNet+DPS-grad eval/step + DC-CG on k in {5,10,15,20,25}). iter-1 ran 214 slices in 1018.96 s at T=25 = 40.8 s/step -> T=28 ~= 40.8*28 + ~5 DC events ~= 1163 s ~= 19.4 min < 20-min wall (1800 s in-solver backstop + 30-min --time as further backstops). T=30 was REJECTED as too tight (~21 min, would blow the hard 20-min budget). val=ALL 214 L277, 321px detector-geometry FOV default.

TRAJECTORY (val=214 L277, 321px FOV, LD-FBP floor ~0.81): iter-1 T=25 SSIM 0.3937/hr0/PSNR14.31; iter-2 eta30->1 -> 0.2366 (REGRESSED, wrong lever); iter-3 relax1.0->0.3 -> 0.2377 (flat, wrong lever); iter-4 T25->28 -> 0.4784/PSNR16.89 (BEST). KEY SIGNAL the iter-4 author under-weighted: T25->T28 MOVED SSIM +0.085 (0.394->0.478) and PSNR +2.6dB (14.3->16.9) MONOTONICALLY -> T is the ONLY live lever and the 25-28 step DDIM schedule is too COARSE for the constrained hard-DC trajectory to converge; eta+relax are exhausted (both regressed when moved off iter-1s working point). advice_for_others: diffusion_recon_dcstep_constrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=40, recon_eta=30.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, recon_dc_solver=cg, val_n=120, train_n=0, rationale=iter-6 search-20260619-01 CONSTRAINED diff-recon — AUDIT CODE-FIX VALIDATION (user-directed 2026-06-20). ONE KNOB: recon_dc_solver legacy->cg (NEW config-gated correct DC path in solver_diffusion_recon.py; legacy path byte-for-byte preserved + reproducible for all prior cfgs). The audit found the legacy DC-step is (1) a MISLABELED steepest-descent dressed as CG (dc_step_cg lines ~83-100) and (2) a re-injection that recomputes x0 from a STALE eps via x0_from_eps(x,eps,ab_next) then re-noises with a FRESH randn mid-schedule (lines ~162-174) — this collapsed unconstrained iter-4 to SSIM 0.055 and kept the constrained variant stuck 0.24-0.66 << the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor at hr=0. THE FIX (ported from the corrected solver_fast_recon.cg_data_consistency): recon_dc_solver=cg swaps in a GENUINE Fletcher-Reeves CG solve of AtA x = At y (residual + conjugate direction + FR beta), forms x0 from the CURRENT step's eps (x0_hat at t_now, not a stale eps re-eval'd at the wrong alpha_bar), CG-projects it, then re-embeds at t_next DETERMINISTICALLY as sqrt(ab_next)*x0_proj_norm + sqrt(1-ab_next)*eps_pred reusing the SAME eps (eps-prediction => the level-t noise direction IS eps_pred) — NO fresh randn, NO stale eps. BASE = iter-5 BEST (T=40, eta=30, relax=1.0, every5/n_cg3/warmup5, val_n=120, SSIM 0.6647/hr0 — the run-best constrained config). Hard DC stays ON (recon_dcstep_every=5) now that it is CORRECT. HONEST EXPECTATION: the corrected CG-DC should STOP the legacy re-noise corruption and likely RAISE SSIM above iter-5's 0.6647 (the deterministic same-eps re-embed no longer overwrites the trajectory with fresh noise + a least-squares fit to the noisy 2304-view LD sinogram). But on DENSE rebinned Mayo (LD-FBP near-complete at 2304 views) the v4 DDPM prior is regime-bounded, so hr may STILL be ~0 — the real payoff is the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks + the planned EMA v5 prior. This iter VALIDATES the fix RUNS and is NON-REGRESSIVE/non-corrupting under the corrected metric. FALSIFIER: if SSIM drops below iter-5's 0.6647 the corrected re-embed is mis-scaling x0 vs eps; if it clears the ~0.81 FBP floor (hr>0) the legacy bug was the whole story. BUDGET: recon_dc_solver=cg is roughly cost-neutral vs legacy (the DPS forward+grad per step is unchanged; the CG inner loop does forward+back per n_cg, comparable to legacy dc_step_cg's forward+back+forward; the deterministic re-embed drops the randn). iter-5 ran T=40 x val_n=120 in 988.0 s = 16.5 min < the HARD 1200s/20-min budget (1800s in-solver backstop + 30-min --time). val_n=120 held at iter-5's value (no reduction needed — 988s leaves ~3.5 min headroom for the CG path's marginal delta). val=120 evenly-spaced L277, 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov=False). staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps single-val-ps probe, bg_target=truth, reuse ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt (NO retrain), 321px FOV.

(5) BUDGET MATH (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): anchored on Mayo bilateral N2I smoke 764666 (n_iter=40, val_n=2, per-image loop elapsed 10.3s => ~5.15 s/scene => ~0.129 s/(iter*scene) on the 2304-view adjoint; ~2x cheaper than the U-Net N2I 9.8 s/scene). Chose n_iter=30 as the sane mid-cost; bilateral cannot overfit so more steps do not hurt. outer_wall_s=1050 (17.5 min) in-solver backstop guarantees a recorded result even if some slices run long; val stays ALL 214 (do NOT reduce val_n). (6) Do NOT return control mid-campaign.

NOT the per-image N2I bilateral variant. SHARES the sibling dual_domain_supervised Mayo path exactly: staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (mayo_per_sample_setup/_fbp, per-sample pipe.R_full swap), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). GOAL: does the bilateral variant RUN on Mayo under the corrected path and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png within the HARD 20-min train+score budget, establishing where the bilateral-supervised baseline lands vs the dual_domain_supervised U-Net (which scored SSIM 0.8880 / hr 0.2759 at c=16/lr=1e-4/ep=8 on the SAME 214-slice 321px-FOV metric, search-20260619-01 iter-1). CONFIG: started from that sibling iter-1 cfg and changed ONLY the image module (U-Net -> bilateral). proj_dn = 1 BF (kernel 3, sx=0.01 along-detector tiny to avoid radial blur, sy=0.3 along-angle, sr=0.0005), img_dn = 3 chained BFs (kernel 5, sx=sy=0.5, sr=0.02) = a SANE MID bilateral depth/kernel (solver default is img_n_bf=1; the discarded boundary-slice TPE hinted img_n_bf=7 which is heavy/over-parameterised for a baseline -- mid=3 establishes the corrected-metric baseline, defer depth as the iter-2 knob). ~24 trainable params total (3 per BF). lr=5e-3 = Wagner BF lr (BF learns scalar sigmas; the U-Net 1e-4 would barely move them in 8 epochs), grad_clip=1.0 kept as a safety on the 2304-view FBP adjoint (the tiny BF params are far less prone to the gradient explosion that forced lr=1e-4 on the U-Net). epochs=8, lambda_neg=1.0, train_n=200 (loader rotates the 4 Wagner train patients ps-pool -> ~400 effective slices/epoch), val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices, batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED by per-sample-ps. This onboarding iter establishes WHERE the bilateral baseline lands under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric; iter-2+ tunes ONE knob (img_n_bf depth first, then the Mayo-specific proj_sr over-smoothing lever).

ONE KNOB: epochs 8->24 (3x). All else identical to iter-1 (proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3 -> 12 trainable params unchanged; 3*(proj_n_bf+img_n_bf)). SIX-BOX: (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.919 / hr 0.0279 in elapsed 254s -- only ~21% of the 1200s (20-min) budget used; 12-param bilateral, lr=5e-3. (2) FAILURE MODE: high SSIM but near-zero hr because the calibrated RMSE-sensitive headroom metric does not credit the bilateral's smoothing (campaign note: SSIM rewards the BF blur, headroom does not). Critically, with only 12 params at lr=5e-3 and 8 epochs the supervised-MSE loss -- which IS RMSE-sensitive, unlike SSIM -- has had little chance to drive the scalar sigmas to their RMSE-optimal (less-smoothing) values: the run is UNDER-TRAINED (254s/1200s). (3) ONE KNOB: epochs 8->24. JUSTIFICATION vs the other candidate (img_n_bf up): adding image-domain bilateral DEPTH at the current loose img_sr=0.02 would smooth MORE, which keeps SSIM high but does NOT lift the RMSE-driven hr (more blur is the wrong direction for headroom); whereas more epochs lets the MSE objective itself pull the sigmas toward the RMSE optimum AND uses the idle ~950s budget. epochs is the cleaner lever for the hr deficit. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if epochs 8->24, then hr rises above 0.0279 (toward the dual_domain_supervised U-Net sibling's 0.276) because the 12 BF sigmas are under-trained at 8 epochs and the supervised-MSE gradient -- being RMSE-sensitive -- will sharpen them. FALSIFIER: if hr stays <=~0.03 (flat) at 24 epochs, the 12-param bilateral is at its CAPACITY ceiling on the 2304-view Mayo FBP (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must instead add capacity (img_n_bf up) or attack the proj-domain over-smoothing (proj_sr) -- epochs is then exhausted. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 254s; per-step cost is dominated by the SHARED 2304-view FBP adjoint, not the 12 BF params, so 24 epochs ~= 3x train ~= 8 epochs*3 plus the single fixed val pass: est ~600-760s << 1200s. Comfortably inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged from iter-1): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (mayo_per_sample_setup/_fbp, per-sample pipe.R_full swap), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override).

SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) iter-1: SSIM 0.8622, hr 0.0, PSNR 33.07 vs baseline_PSNR 34.08 (recon is BELOW the LD-FBP baseline), RMSE 1.11e-3, elapsed 971.99s (16.2 min). Measured from the [fit] log: per-scan fit loop = 214 scenes x 15 steps in 846.9s -> 0.264 s/per-scan-step = 3.96 s/scene; fixed overhead (1 warm-start epoch ~50s + dataset setup + scoring + figure ~75s) = 125.1s. (2) FAILURE MODE: hr=0, recon PSNR 33.07 < FBP 34.08 -> the per-scan fit is INIT-DOMINATED. At only 15 per-scan Adam steps the per-image recon has barely left the warm-start U-Net init, so the result is essentially the (1-epoch, under-trained) warm-start applied per scan -- below baseline. This is starvation of the INIT, not over-fit (the over-fit / lr-down regime is at n_iter 600-1200, far above here). (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 1->4 (n_iter=15, lr=1e-3, grad_clip=1.0, unet_c=16, val_n=214, seed=42 ALL HELD). Why pretrain_epochs and not n_iter: the 214-scene budget HARD-CAPS n_iter -- at 0.264 s/step, a 19-min (1140s) total leaves 1015s of fit time -> 1015/(214*0.264) = 17.9 steps, so n_iter can only go 15->17 (+13%, too marginal to test). lr-down is wrong-signed (that lever is for the OVER-fit high-n_iter regime; here we are UNDER baseline). warm_start is LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE (confirmed cross-substrate) and the init is the anchor the 15-step fit refines, so DEEPENING the warm-start is the highest-leverage in-budget move. (4) HYPOTHESIS: pretrain_epochs 1->4 lifts SSIM above 0.8622 and ideally hr above 0 (PSNR above the 34.08 FBP baseline), because a deeper warm-start gives a better U-Net init that the fixed 15 per-scan steps refine from -- the recon stops being dominated by an under-trained 1-epoch init. FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.8622 (no gain or regression), the warm-start init is NOT the binding constraint and per-image N2I is structurally FBP-bounded on dense 2304-view Mayo (half-view info loss > the per-image denoising gain) -> iter-3 documents the structural floor (NAF/ram class) rather than tuning further. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min, val=ALL 214): warm-start 4 epochs x ~50s = 200s (+150s vs iter-1) + fit loop UNCHANGED 846.9s + fixed setup/score/figure ~75s = 1121.9s = 18.7 min < 1200s/20-min hard wall (~78s margin). The fit loop is unchanged so its outer_wall_s=1080 in-solver backstop is unchanged; the warm-start is outside that wall and outside the budgeted [fit] timer. n_iter NOT raised (budget-capped). val_n=214 NOT reduced (protocol). PER-IMAGE structure unchanged. (6) no control return.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_supervised-claude-agentic: unet_c=16, lr=0.0001, epochs=8, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 feasibility (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). GOAL: does dual_domain_supervised run on Mayo under the corrected path (staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP + per-sample pipe.R_full swap, bg_target=truth) and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png within the HARD 20-min train+score budget, scoring ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override)? This is the SUPERVISED dual-domain U-Net (proj_dn -> FBP(full views) -> img_dn, MSE-vs-truth + lambda_neg negativity penalty), NOT the per-image N2I variant. CONFIG: two SmallUNet denoisers (proj + img) at c=16 (~1.0M params total), lr=1e-4 (the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients ~18x vs demo's 128 views -> lr=5e-4 NaNs ep1 / lr=1e-4 NaNs ep2 standalone, so grad_clip=1.0 + nonfinite-grad-skip is MANDATORY and lr is kept conservative), epochs=8, lambda_neg=1.0 (validated-stable standalone default; the discarded boundary-slice run hinted lambda_neg=0.1 as best -- treat as behavior hint only, defer the knob to iter-2+). batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 are FORCED by the per-sample-ps path (each train step swaps pipe.R_full to its slice ps; each val slice does likewise). train_n=200 stratified across the 4 Wagner train patients' ps-groups (loader rotates the full pool -> ~400 effective slices/epoch). val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices. SIZING: itnet_v3 (heavier -- k=3 unrolled DC steps) iter-1 trained 8 epochs + scored all 214 slices in 738s (~12.3 min) under this same sbatch wall; DD-UNet has no unrolled DC loop so it is CHEAPER per step -> 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure fits comfortably inside the 20-min budget (30-min sbatch wall). HYPOTHESIS: dual_domain_supervised at c=16/lr=1e-4/ep=8 on ~200-400 stratified Mayo train slices trains stably (no NaN, grad-clip+skip holds) and produces a finite val_ssim that CLEARS the LD-FBP baseline (hr>0), because a supervised dual-domain (sinogram + image U-Net) denoiser of the full-view FBP is a strong Mayo recon family (loose hint from the discarded boundary-slice run: ~0.96 SSIM with epochs as the lever -- NOT a validated number under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (epochs first, then lambda_neg).

ONE KNOB: CAPACITY unet_c 16 -> 24 (the two SmallUNet denoisers proj_dn+img_dn both widen; params ~0.466M -> ~1.05M, a (24/16)^2=2.25x conv-compute bump), with epochs TRADED DOWN 27 -> 10 to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. SIX-BOX. (1) NUMBERS: iter-2 ep20/c16 SSIM 0.909762 hr 0.338985; iter-3 ep27/c16 SSIM 0.918191 hr 0.365357 (CHAMPION) in elapsed_s=1151.4; current config unet_c=16 epochs=27 lr=1e-4. (2) LIMITER: the epochs lever WORKS (monotone hr ep8 0.276 -> ep20 0.339 -> ep27 0.3654) but is now WALL-LOCKED: iter-3 ep27 used 1151.4s of the 1200s budget; the iter-3 note computed ep32 -> 1366s BUSTS the wall, so epochs cannot rise. The other budget-free lever, an lr-schedule, is NOT WIRED in solver_dual_ddomain_supervised.py (opt=torch.optim.Adam(lr=cfg['lr']) at line 151, no scheduler/weight_decay) and adding one would require editing a SHARED solver (FORBIDDEN). So the only legitimate single-knob iter-4 lever is CAPACITY (unet_c, wired at line 141 -> both denoisers). Is the champion capacity-limited? iter-3's own falsifier said 'if hr <= 0.339 at ep27 -> capacity-limited'; hr ROSE to 0.3654 instead, so it is still PARTLY training-limited, NOT cleanly capacity-limited -> trading epochs down is a genuine gamble, which is exactly what this iter tests. (3) ONE KNOB: unet_c 16->24, epochs 27->10. BUDGET-TRADE MATH: from the two measured c16 points per_epoch=(893.06-418.58)/(20-8)=39.5s/epoch, fixed (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O)=418.58-8*39.5=102.6s (iter-3 ep27 predicted 1169s vs actual 1151.4s, calibration good). A c16->c24 widening multiplies the U-Net portion of compute by (24/16)^2=2.25x; the per-sample 2304-view FBP adjoint is c-INDEPENDENT, so the REALISTIC per-epoch at c24 (assuming ~30pct of per-epoch is the c-independent FBP adjoint) is 39.5*(0.30+0.70*2.25)=74.1s and realistic fixed (val ~half c-scaling) ~166s -> ep10 realistic = 166+10*74.1=908s (~15.1 min, comfortably inside 1200s). The WORST-CASE upper bound (pessimistically assume EVERYTHING incl. the FBP adjoint scales 2.25x): per_epoch_worst=39.5*2.25=89.0s, fixed_worst=102.6*2.25=230.9s -> ep10 worst = 230.9+10*89.0=1120s < 1200s -> FITS even the worst case. ep12 worst=1298s BUSTS, so without a measured c24 timing point ep10 is the LARGEST epoch count guaranteed to fit; epochs is sized to the worst-case bound, not the optimistic one (a wall-bust wastes the whole QOS slot). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 2.25x more representational capacity lifts hr above the iter-3 champion 0.365357 even at the reduced ep10, because the DD-UNet is a strong recon family and the discarded boundary-slice run loosely hinted c=24 was its best capacity (TPE: c=24, ep=18, hr 0.836 under that bad metric -- behavior hint only). FALSIFIER (in NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.365 at unet_c=24/ep10, the DD-UNet has hit its representational ceiling on this val set (~0.37) AND/OR ep10 under-trained the bigger net more than the capacity helped -> document the champion ceiling; iter-5 would then either (a) keep c24 and recover epochs toward the wall if c24 per-epoch is measured to be cheaper than the worst case (i.e. ep10 left budget headroom), or (b) revert to c16/ep27 and accept 0.3654 as the DD-UNet ceiling. advice_for_others: fast-diffusion pixel/unconstrained: on dense full-view Mayo, an 8-step diffusion-prior recon clears FBP on SSIM (0.8745 > 0.8147) but stays PSNR/RMSE-bounded below the LD-FBP floor on the calibrated metric -> hr 0.0; the larger 'unconstrained' train pool lifts SSIM ~0.013 over the constrained prior (0.8615) but does NOT clear the FBP headroom floor on this dense-view geometry.
rationale: fast-diffusion recon (pixel domain, unconstrained prior): per-image few-step DC-guided reconstruction from a trained fast-diffusion prior (solver_fast_recon.py, 8-step, FBP init @ t=0.7, eta=1.0, DC=1 CG=5). The 'unconstrained' prior was trained on the larger Mayo train slice pool (vs the 50-slice constrained prior); 'unconstrained' is a misnomer inherited from the demo-dl phantom regime and means MORE train slices, NOT GT leakage (train split only; no val/test). Evaluated on ALL 214 L277 Mayo val slices under the calibrated-SSIM-headroom metric (baseline LD-FBP SSIM 0.8147 / PSNR 34.08 dB; oracle HD-FBP). Result: SSIM 0.8745, PSNR 31.20 dB, calibrated headroom 0.0000. Honest negative on headroom: SSIM clears LD-FBP (0.8147) but the RMSE/PSNR-sensitive calibrated metric keeps PSNR (31.20 dB) below the LD-FBP floor (34.08 dB) on dense (2304-view) rebinned Mayo -> hr pinned at 0.0 (FBP-bounded, below-baseline). Cluster eval run: recon-fast-diffusion-pixel_unconstrained-766045; checkpoint /cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_unconstrained.pt (final_val_flow_loss 0.0162).

rationale: fast-diffusion recon (wavelet domain, constrained DC): per-image few-step DC-guided reconstruction from a trained fast-diffusion prior (solver_fast_recon.py, 8-step, FBP init @ t=0.7, eta=1.0, DC=1 CG=5). advice_for_others: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=40, batch_size=4, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1080, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY under the corrected protocol (val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget). Hammernik-2017 here is an IMAGE-DOMAIN variational net that denoises the FBP -- NO projector inside the unrolled loop, so each forward is far cheaper than LPD (which ran the PYRO-NN projector in-loop and still did train200+score214 in 1149s/19.2min). That cheapness is spent on CONVERGENCE not capacity, to dodge the LPD trap (under-trained heavy unrolled net -> hr=0 @ SSIM 0.843). Capacity modest: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default for a cheaper RBF activation loop), vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31; vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 = the documented VN-port working corner (LOOSE hint, not validated). Training favors convergence: epochs=40, train_n=200, batch=4, lr=5e-4, grad_clip=1.0; max_train_s=1080 (18min) in-solver wall trips before the 30min SLURM kill, leaving headroom for score(214)+figure. Hyp: a budget-sized, ACTUALLY-CONVERGED Hammernik-2017 lands near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP-ish SSIM floor within 20 min on Mayo; if even at 40 epochs it stays stuck at hr=0 with lambda_t barely budging (the documented 2026-06-08 failure signature), that is the iter-1 feasibility finding -- a shared-filter-bank structural ceiling, not a config knob away.

advice_for_others: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=search-20260619-01 iter-2 OOM RESCUE of hammernik_2017. iter-1 (batch_size=4) was NOT a real recon: it CUDA-OOMed in the _rho_prime RBF-bump loop at elapsed_s=72.5 on a 16GB RTX5000 (val_score blank in results.tsv), recorded as 0.0. The (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF activation tensors held across 5 unrolled steps for autograd blew the card. SINGLE COHERENT memory-safety change for this rescue: batch_size 4->2, which halves every per-batch activation tensor in the bump loop -- the direct cause. NOTE: this hammernik_2017 solver is a PURE IMAGE-DOMAIN denoiser of the FBP (no projector in the unrolled loop) and does NOT read vn_checkpoint or vn_dc_norm (verified by grep over every cfg[...]/cfg.get(...) in the solver: only vn_T/vn_n_filters/vn_kernel/vn_n_bumps/vn_x_range/vn_*_init_std/vn_lambda_init/epochs/batch_size/lr/grad_clip/train_n/val_n/seed/max_train_s are consumed). Those two knobs belong to the SIBLING projector-in-loop hammernik_vn solver; passing them here would be silently ignored, so they are intentionally omitted -- the operative fix this solver honors is the batch halving (+ grad_clip=1.0 already present for VN-family NaN-skip stability). advice_for_others: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_2017 iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: vn_lambda_init 0.0023 -> 0.05 (~22x DC-weight init). All else held at iter-2 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=5e-4, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42). PRIOR (NUMBERS, corrected metric): iter-1 OOM at batch_size=4 (no recon, hr=0, elapsed 72s); iter-2 = FIRST valid datapoint, val_ssim=0.80123 hr=0 (PSNR 33.91, RMSE 0.00101, baseline_PSNR 34.08 so LD-FBP floor SSIM ~0.84; iter-2 is BELOW the FBP floor), elapsed 887s (train 789.7s, ~5 min budget headroom under the 30-min SLURM kill). iter-1->iter-2 = the first finite point; this is hammernik_2017's first real number under the corrected metric and it sits below baseline. DIAGNOSIS from iter-2 SLURM log 765262: training CONVERGED (loss 2.5e-4 ep1 -> 8.7e-7 ep14, flat by ep5) so epochs-up is INERT (NOT under-training); and CRITICALLY lambda_t stayed pinned at ['0.0023','0.00231','0.00232','0.00232','0.00233'] across ALL 14 epochs -- Adam never grew the learnable DC weight from its init. HYPOTHESIS: with the DC anchor ~22x stronger, val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor and hr>0 (predict val_ssim > 0.84). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the lambda VALUE does not change per-step compute (same image-domain conv + RBF-bump loop), so cost ~= iter-2: train ~790s + ~100s score(214)+figure ~= 890s, well under the 1800s SLURM kill. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-2 -- batch_size=2 (KEPT, do NOT raise: bs=4 OOMed the 16GB card in the _rho_prime RBF-bump loop at iter-1) + N_k=16 + 31-bump activation across 5 unrolled steps stays within 16 GB. grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability).

Per the prompt's explicit fallback and iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier, iter-4 attacks the REGULARIZER ITSELF via the leanest config that avoids the DC-smoothing collapse: ONE KNOB vn_n_filters 16 -> 4 (shrink the analysis-filter bank 4x). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=5e-4, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, corrected metric, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 OOM at batch_size=4 (no recon, elapsed 72s); iter-2 SSIM 0.80123 (FIRST valid datapoint, PSNR 33.91, RMSE 0.00101, baseline_PSNR 34.08, elapsed 887s); iter-3 SSIM 0.793173 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.008, PSNR 33.92, RMSE 0.001007, elapsed 895.8s). FAILURE MODE (well-characterized, confirmed cross-sibling): the learned VN regularizer term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i y) (solver line 141) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init y_NN below baseline, and at iter-3 lambda_t stayed pinned at init across all 14 epochs (Adam never grew the DC weight), so the lambda-anchor cannot save it. The sibling hammernik_vn shows the SAME signature: iter-1 0.8053 -> iter-2 0.7920 (filters UP regressed) -> iter-3 0.7682 (lambda UP regressed), monotone below FBP. ONE KNOB CHOICE: vn_n_filters 16 -> 4 is the most-diagnostic remaining regularizer attack in THIS solver. Shrinking the analysis-filter bank 4x structurally minimizes the degrees of freedom of the smoothing term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i y) -- the leanest learned-regularizer that still leaves a learned term at all. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation is the over-parameterized 16-filter bank collapsing into a low-pass smoother of the FBP init, a 4-filter bank has far less capacity to over-smooth -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init. (x_range/kernel held; n_filters is the single cleanest capacity-of-the-regularizer knob.) HYPOTHESIS: with the filter bank shrunk 16->4, the regularizer stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0); predict val_ssim > 0.84. FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the leanest regularizer, then hammernik_2017 (and the whole VN family -- the sibling hammernik_vn is exhausting capacity + DC weight + filter-normalization in parallel) is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on real 2304-view rebinned Mayo LDCT regardless of regularizer config -> FILE THE NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik learned-regularizer family does not beat LD-FBP on Mayo. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): FEWER filters means CHEAPER per-step compute (conv over 4 instead of 16 channels + 4-channel RBF-bump loop), so wall <= iter-3 (895.8s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, >900s margin. advice_for_others: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY (corrected protocol: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-step model.projector swap, bg_target=truth, no fov= override). Hammernik-VN = MRI variational net ported to CT: T untied unrolled steps, each = learned filter-bank + per-filter RBF activation (the _rho_prime bump loop) PLUS an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step (architectural twin of LPD/ItNet but tiny interpretable regulariser). CRITICAL LESSON from the SIBLING hammernik_2017 iter-1: it did NOT diverge to 0.0 -- it CUDA-OOM'd in _rho_prime at 72s with batch_size=4 (16GB RTX5000; the (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF tensors + 5-step autograd blew the card). So the dominant iter-1 risk here is MEMORY, not divergence. MITIGATION: batch_size=2 (NOT 4), vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default -> fewer RBF tensors), vn_checkpoint=true (gradient-checkpoints each unrolled step -- hammernik_vn HAS this knob, cuts activation memory ~T-fold; this is the key difference that lets the projector-in-loop VN fit where the 2017 batch=4 did not). STABILITY against the documented VN family divergence/NaN->0.0 trap: grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY -- the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward; clip_and_step also SKIPS nonfinite-gradient batches so a poisoned step can't collapse the recon to a constant), vn_dc_norm=true (power-iter normalizes R^T(Rx-g) so softplus(lambda_t) stays O(1) regardless of geometry -- the safeguard the projector-less 2017 lacked), lr=5e-4 (the documented hammernik_vn optimum from the discarded run; 8e-4 was worse, brief caps lr<=5e-4), vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 (loose VN-port working-corner hint). CAPACITY conservative per brief: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0 (FBP recon is ~O(1) so the RBF grid [-1,1] covers it). BUDGET: reference -- LPD (projector-in-loop, T=7, ep30, train200, score214) ran 1150s/19.2min right at the edge; hammernik_vn at T=5/N_k=16/checkpointed should be comparable-or-cheaper per step. max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the BINDING constraint (epochs=14 is just an upper bound the wall trips first), leaving ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill. HYPOTHESIS: if I run a budget-sized, MEMORY-SAFE (batch=2, checkpointed), STABLE (grad_clip=1.0, dc_norm) Hammernik-VN, I expect (a) it AVOIDS the hammernik_2017 OOM and produces a FINITE val_ssim within 20min, and (b) the projector DC step lands it near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP SSIM floor -- because a learned-regulariser + true-projector-DC unroll is a sound Mayo recon family (sibling LPD/ItNet/DD-sup all run finite here). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric VN baseline that iter-2+ tunes one knob at a time (epochs/wall first to confirm convergence, then vn_T or vn_lambda_init).

LAST-LEVER / confirmation iter. ONE KNOB on the REGULARIZER (not capacity, not lambda): vn_normalize_filters False -> True (constrain each learned filter K_i to zero-mean + unit-norm, the paper-faithful constraint, solver _effective_weight lines 119-128). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_lambda_init=0.05, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, elapsed 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, elapsed 1159.6s, val_psnr 32.07, val_rmse 1.246e-3). BOTH structural levers already attacked the wrong thing: capacity-UP regressed AND DC-weight-UP regressed, so the recon sits monotonically BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). FAILURE MODE (well-characterized): the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline, and it does so REGARDLESS of capacity (filters^ hurt) or DC weight (lambda^ hurt). This FIRES iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier: 'if SSIM stays <=0.84 under strong DC, the VN regulariser is structurally degrading -> iter-4 attacks the regulariser itself: vn_normalize_filters=True OR vn_init=backproj'. CHOICE OF KNOB (most diagnostic remaining): vn_normalize_filters=True is the SHARPEST test of the smoothing diagnosis, and is preferred over vn_init=backproj (which changes only the init, not the regularizer mechanism, and the baseline is pinned to FBP either way). MECHANISM: zero-mean filters have NO DC response -- conv with a zero-mean kernel annihilates any uniform/low-frequency level component -- so a zero-mean-unit-norm-constrained K_i CANNOT apply a uniform smoothing or level shift to the image; the regulariser term can only act on local CONTRAST (edges/texture).
