SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR RESULTS: iter-1 ep8 -> SSIM 0.4413 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 20.44 / RMSE 0.004756, elapsed 191.1s; iter-2 ep48 -> SSIM 0.5927 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 24.77 / RMSE 0.002886, elapsed 387.4s. The pretrain_epochs lever moves SSIM (0.4413->0.5927, +0.151 over 8->48 ep) but hr stays PINNED at 0.000 -- v1 is still BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor after a 6x pretrain increase. CONTRAST: the lever-twin itnet_v2 (same pretrain-then-DC family) climbed ep48 0.5888 -> ep144 0.6230 (3x epochs for only +0.034 SSIM, hr still 0.000 -- severe diminishing returns), while the END-TO-END-trained sibling itnet_v3 sits at 0.905 / hr 0.312 at iter-3. v1 (0.44->0.59) and v2 (0.59->0.62) trace the SAME under-0.81 curve; v3 (0.91) is on a different curve entirely. (2) LIMITER = the pretrain-then-FIXED-DC CEILING (structural, confirmed by reading solver_itnet.py): finetune_itnet() is DEFINED (lines 114-135) but NEVER called in main(); the k=3 ItNet DC unroll (forward, lines 76-90) has ZERO trainable parameters of its own (self.alpha is a plain float, self.projector is fixed analytic PYRO-NN); itnet.eval()+torch.no_grad() (lines 208-209) run the unroll as pure INFERENCE. The ONLY trainable component is the standalone SmallUNet denoiser (params_M=0.2329, exactly the UNet), pretrained as an FBP->truth denoiser that NEVER sees the DC steps during training. So pretrain_epochs is the sole lever and the fixed untrained DC post-processor caps v1 far below the end-to-end v3. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48 -> 160 (3.3x), mirroring v2's 48->144 ceiling-probe escalation. All else identical to iter-2 (k=3, itnet_alpha=0.005, unet_c=16, pretrain_lr=1e-4, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: a final hard push of the only trainable component. FALSIFIER (the operative one): if SSIM stays well below the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor and far below v3's 0.91 (predicted ~0.63-0.66, tracking v2's flattening 0.62 at comparable epochs), itnet v1 is STRUCTURALLY pretrain-then-fixed-DC-capped -- NOT under-trained -- and the campaign should document this ceiling and direct future Mayo recon to itnet_v3 (end-to-end unrolled, 0.91) rather than spend more iters on v1's epochs lever. The counter-hypothesis (v1 suddenly clears 0.81 at 160 ep) is implausible given the +0.151 then +0.034-class diminishing slope already measured. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): from the two measured points the per-epoch pretrain cost is (387.4-191.1)/(48-8) = 4.91 s/epoch and the fixed cost (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure + startup) is 191.1 - 8*4.91 = 151.8 s. pretrain_epochs=160 predicts 151.8 + 160*4.91 = 937 s = 15.6 min, comfortably inside the 1200s budget with margin for val-pass variance; pretrain_epochs=200 would predict 1134s (18.9 min, too tight), so 160 is a safe decisive push. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside the DC step overflows otherwise). v1 has NO max_train_s backstop (not in the solver), so the 30-min sbatch wall is the only hard fence -- 15.6 min predicted leaves ample headroom. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. advice_for_others: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.0001, pretrain_epochs=12, pretrain_patience=12, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=900, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 feasibility (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). itnet_v2 onboarding. CONFIG: residual_learning=False (MANDATORY: the CONFIG default True double-applies the residual -- SmallUNet.forward already returns x-body(x), then ItNetV2.forward re-adds denoiser(x) -> ~2x at eval which the k DC steps cannot recover, stuck ~0.34; False matches the working v1/v3 recipe). Shared ItNet architecture seeded from itnet_v3 iter-1 (0.896 SSIM / hr0.268 under the SAME corrected metric): itnet_k=3 DC steps, unet_c=16 SmallUNet denoiser, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037 (TV-lambda, learnable), grad_clip=1.0 (mandatory: 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside dc_step overflows otherwise), seed=42. TRAINING uses v2 pretrain knobs (v2 pre-trains the denoiser then applies k=3 DC at eval; it is NOT end-to-end like v3): pretrain_lr=1e-4 (v3 unstable above; mirror), pretrain_epochs=12, pretrain_patience=12 (disable the 1pct early-stop so the full budget converges -- AVOID the v1 0.441 under-training trap). batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 are FORCED by per-sample-ps (each slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps). train_n=200 -> 200 steps/epoch. val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices -- do NOT reduce). max_train_s=900 (15 min) HARD backstop so train leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the 30-min wall. HYPOTHESIS: itnet_v2 with residual_learning=False at k=3/c=16/lr=1e-4 for 12 pretrain epochs on 200 stratified Mayo train slices produces a finite val_ssim that CLEARS the LD-FBP baseline (hr>0) and lands in the ~0.88-0.90 SSIM band like its siblings, because a pretrained denoiser + k=3 DC-step refinement of the per-sample-ps FBP is a strong Mayo recon family and the residual_learning=False fix removes the double-residual collapse. This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (pretrain_epochs first).

advice_for_others: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.0001, pretrain_epochs=48, pretrain_patience=48, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=960, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48 (4x); pretrain_patience tracked 12->48 so the early-stop never fires before the full 48 epochs (same disable-early-stop intent as iter-1, where patience==epochs). All else identical to iter-1 (k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); only max_train_s 900->960 to admit the longer pretrain inside the wall. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 (val_psnr 21.24, val_rmse 0.00434) in elapsed_s=170.2 -- only ~14% of the 1200s (20-min) train+score budget used; pretrain_epochs=12. (2) FAILURE MODE: the pretrain-denoiser-then-data-consistency path UNDER-CONVERGES in the budget (same as v1, which was stuck at 0.441). The k=3 DC steps refine a denoiser that has not yet learned the Mayo image statistics; SSIM 0.455 is far below the end-to-end itnet_v3 sibling (0.896). With only 12 pretrain epochs at lr=1e-4 the denoiser is under-trained, and 170s/1200s proves the budget was almost entirely idle. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48, mirroring the SIBLING itnet (v1) iter-2 which raised pretrain_epochs 8->48 and jumped SSIM 0.441->0.593 (+0.15) under THIS campaign and metric -- the strongest just-proven signal that pretraining was the v1/v2 bottleneck. Chosen over lr-up (v3 is unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe v1 move) and over architecture knobs (k/unet_c) which would change the model not the convergence. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if pretrain_epochs 12->48, val_ssim rises substantially above 0.4554 (toward v1 iter-2's ~0.59, possibly the ~0.88-0.90 sibling band) because more pretraining lets the denoiser converge before the k=3 DC refinement, exactly as it did for v1. FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays flat (<=~0.47) at 48 epochs, the pretrain-DC architecture is CAPPED in this budget regardless of pretraining (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must move toward end-to-end unrolled training (the v3 recipe) or accept the pretrain-DC path is budget-limited. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 12 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 170s; the per-epoch pretrain cost over 200 stratified slices is the variable part and the 214-slice per-sample val + figure are roughly fixed. 4x the epochs is roughly 4x the small pretrain base plus the single fixed val/figure pass: est well under 600s, far below 1200s; max_train_s=960 is a 16-min HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged from iter-1): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override). residual_learning=False KEPT (the CONFIG default True double-applies the residual and collapses eval to ~0.34).

SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=12 in elapsed_s=170.2; iter-2 = SSIM 0.5888 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=48 in elapsed_s=345.2. Trajectory: 4x epochs (12->48) lifted SSIM +0.133, still hr=0 (FBP floor ~0.81, far above). v3 SIBLING (same ItNet family, END-TO-END unrolled, no pretrain-DC) reaches SSIM 0.91 -- the contrast that frames v2's limiter. DATA-COVERAGE lever on the BOARD CHAMPION. ONE KNOB: train_n 400->579 (FULL 579-slice train pool, ~69%->100% coverage), with pretrain_epochs traded 120->72 + pretrain_patience tracked 120->72 (early-stop stays disabled) to HOLD the HARD 1200s wall AND keep grad-step parity train_n*epochs (iter-7 400*120=48000; iter-8 579*72=41688, ~13% fewer steps as a budget-safety margin since iter-7 overran at 1308.6s). Base=iter-7 (the BREAKOUT, NEW #1, SSIM 0.9414/hr 0.4187 @itnet_k=1/tn400/ep120). KEEP itnet_k=1 (the iter-7 breakout) and residual_learning=False (the mandatory config-fix). MECHANISM (campaign_state.md, CONFIRMED): build_dataset calls load_val_split(split='train', n=train_n) -> a FIXED n-slice subset loaded ONCE; pretrain_denoiser merely reshuffles that subset each epoch (torch.randperm), NO RotatingSubsetDataset. So train_n=400 lets the denoiser see only ~69% of the 579-slice pool (3 ps-groups: 154@0.66192, 98@0.73979, 327@0.77873); train_n=579 raises coverage to 100%. This is the SAME confirmed lever that lifted uswin (200->480, hr 0.3532->0.3829, +0.0297) and itnet_v3 (200->400, hr 0.3123->0.3288, +0.0165) and itnet v1 (200->300). CURRENT train_n=400 (~69% of 579 pool). (2) LIMITER: with itnet_k=1 unlocked, the binding limiter is now the TRAINED DENOISER's data coverage -- it only sees ~69% of the anatomy in the 579-slice pool because the fixed-subset loader never rotates. The single trained-denoiser+1-DC pass is excellent (0.9414) but the denoiser is data-coverage-limited, the proven climb lever for the end-to-end/denoiser trainers this campaign. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 400->579 (full pool), pretrain_epochs traded 120->72 to hold budget; itnet_k=1 KEPT, residual_learning=False KEPT. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if train_n 400->579, val_ssim/hr rises ABOVE iter-7 0.4187 because the denoiser sees 100% vs 69% of the 579-slice anatomical variety at near-equal optimization, exactly as full-coverage lifted uswin/itnet_v3/v1. NUMERIC FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.4187 (flat/down) at train_n=579, the denoiser is NOT data-coverage-limited at k=1 -- coverage is exhausted -- and iter-9 reverts to tn400 and probes pretrain_epochs UP (more denoiser convergence) as the next lever. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score. iter-7 per-epoch at tn400/k1 ~8.31s/epoch, fixed (214-slice per-sample val + figure) ~312s (1308.6 - 120*8.31). At tn579 per-epoch ~8.31*579/400=12.03s/epoch -> 72 ep: 72*12.03 + 312 = 1178s, UNDER 1200s (and grad-steps 41688 < 48000 gives extra margin vs iter-7's overrun). max_train_s=1050 (17.5-min HARD backstop) GUARANTEES the 214-slice per-sample val + figure finish inside the 30-min sbatch wall, ending the overrun risk. val_n=214 KEPT (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT, batch_size=2 (itnet_v2 needs bs=2 per six-box) -- NOTE solver FORCES bs=1+val_chunk=1 via per-sample-ps so this is moot. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. The epochs-up lever is CONFIRMED (hr +0.0416, monotone over 8->14 ep) -> itnet_v3 is STILL UNDER-TRAINED, not capacity-limited (iter-2 falsifier hr<=0.268 did NOT trigger). (2) LIMITER NOW = the 20-min train+score wall, NOT convergence: iter-2 used 16.83/20 min. (3) ONE KNOB: epochs 14 -> 18 (~29pct more gradient steps). START FROM iter-3 BEST (c16/ep18, hr 0.3123), NOT iter-4's regressed c24. ONE KNOB: train_n 200 -> 400 (TRAINING DATA = the one untried lever), with epochs traded DOWN 18 -> 9 to (a) hold total gradient steps at PARITY with iter-3 best (400*9 = 3600 = 200*18) so any hr change isolates DATA COVERAGE, not extra optimization, and (b) fit the HARD 20-min train+score wall. All else = iter-3 best exactly (itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=1e-4, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (2) LIMITER: epochs PLATEAUED (iter-2 ep14 hr 0.3101 -> iter-3 ep18 hr 0.3123, +0.0022, SSIM even dropped) AND capacity-for-epochs REGRESSED (iter-4). The remaining limiter is DATA COVERAGE: the itnet_v3 solver loads a FIXED stratified train subset ONCE via build_dataset -> load_val_split(split='train', n=train_n) (solver_itnet_v3.py lines 198-199) and merely RESHUFFLES that same subset every epoch (torch.randperm(train_n), line 235). It does NOT use RotatingSubsetDataset, so train_n=200 means the net has only ever seen 200 of the 579 available train slices -> data-coverage-limited. train_n IS load-bearing here (NOT inert): the full pool is 579 slices across 3 ps-groups/patients (154 @0.66192, 98 @0.73979, 327 @0.77873); train_n=200 used only 35pct of it. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 200 -> 400 (2x distinct slices = 69pct of the 579-slice pool; the stratified round-robin spans all 3 train patients more densely). epochs traded 18 -> 9 to fund it at grad-step parity (3600). (4) HYPOTHESIS: doubling distinct training slices (200 -> 400) lifts hr above the 0.3123 iter-3 best, because itnet_v3 is data-coverage-limited (epochs + capacity both exhausted) and a denser, more representative train set generalises better to the held-out L277 val patient. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.3123 at train_n=400 (all else iter-3-best, grad steps held at 3600), itnet_v3 is at its budget-constrained ceiling (~0.31) on this 214-slice / 321px-FOV Mayo val set with ALL three levers (epochs, capacity, data) exhausted -> iter-6 would have to change the metric basis or accept the ceiling. Per-epoch scales LINEARLY with train_n (bs=1 -> train_n steps/epoch), so train_n=400 -> per-epoch 68.9 s. At epochs=9: 481.0 + 9*68.9 = 1101 s = 18.35 min < 1200 s with ~99 s headroom. epochs=10 -> 1170 s = 19.5 min (tight); epochs=9 is the safe largest count at train_n=400 that also holds grad-step parity. On DENSE 2304-view Mayo the LD-FBP is NEAR-COMPLETE (2304 views >> Nyquist; well-conditioned operator), so there is NO ill-posedness headroom for the unrolled updates to exploit -> LPD sharpens structure (rising SSIM) but cannot push RMSE below the already-near-optimal LD-FBP -> hr=0 regardless of capacity/epochs/lr/data. REMAINING UNTRIED AXIS = unroll DEPTH itself: lpd_iters 3->5 doubles-ish the learned primal-dual correction steps. If Mayo had ANY FBP-incompleteness headroom, deeper unrolling (the thing that makes LPD an unrolled net, not a U-Net) is exactly where it would surface. BUDGET MATH vs 1200s: iters=5 raises per-sample projector fwd+adj cost ~5/3x vs iters=3, so epochs traded 10->6 AND train_n 300->200 to hold the wall. FALSIFIER: hr stays 0.000 (and SSIM <= 0.898 since ep6 under-trains vs iter-4 ep10) => deeper unrolling does NOT help => DEFINITIVE structural ceiling: dense 2304-view LD-FBP is near-complete, LPD has no ill-posedness to exploit, FBP-bounded regardless of unroll depth. advice_for_others: manduca_bilateral-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=six-box: (a) iter-1 hr=0.0598 ssim=0.9243 (positive-headroom) at paper-faithful defaults proj_n_bf=1, proj_sr=1.5, bf_d_w_ratio=1/6, manduca_N0=1e5, img_n_bf=1, ep=10, ~387s. (b) Limiter: under-smoothing in the projection (Q=sqrt(N0*exp(-P))) domain. With N0=1e5, Q in [0,~316] and the sqrt/Anscombe noise std ~0.5 sqrt-counts; proj_sr=1.5 only averages pixels within +/-1.5 sqrt-counts so the dominant mid-Q soft-tissue noise (where Mayo SSIM is gated) survives into the FBP. Tiny capacity (~7 params) means the range bandwidth IS the denoising strength. (c) Lever: proj_sr 1.5 -> 3.0 (one knob) widens the range kernel to ~6 noise-sigma so the proj-bilateral averages more surviving soft-tissue noise, raising calibrated-SSIM-headroom. (d) No capacity/epoch change -> same ~387s wall, well inside 20-min budget. (e) BASE_ITER=1., proj_sr=3.0

advice_for_others: manduca_bilateral-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=six-box manduca_bilateral iter-3 (EXPLORATORY). (a) PRIOR: iter-1 (proj_sr=1.5) hr=0.05982; iter-2 (proj_sr=3.0) hr=0.05978 -> proj_sr FLAT (range bandwidth NOT the binding constraint over 1.5-3.0). (b) FAILURE MODE: the proj-bilateral spatial footprint is sub-pixel. With proj_w=5 and bf_d_w_ratio=1/6, proj spatial sigma = (1/6)*5 = 0.83 px < 1 px, so the kernel averages essentially only the center detector sample. No matter how wide the RANGE kernel (proj_sr) is opened, there are no spatial neighbors being pooled, so soft-tissue noise survives into the FBP and hr is pinned. The range bandwidth can only bite once the spatial reach covers real neighbors. (c) LEVER (one knob): bf_d_w_ratio 1/6(=0.167) -> 0.5, raising proj spatial sigma 0.83px -> 2.5px (a genuine ~5-tap pooling footprint), which finally lets the already-wide range kernel average surviving mid-Q soft-tissue noise -> higher calibrated-SSIM-headroom. This is the paper-locked d/w degree of freedom, the highest-impact lever given the tiny (~7-param) capacity where kernel geometry IS the denoising strength. (d) BUDGET: no capacity/epoch change -> ~387-557s wall as in iter-1/2, well inside the 20-min budget. (e) BASE_ITER=1 (hr-best; iter-2 is tied within noise)., bf_d_w_ratio=0.5

advice_for_others: manduca_bilateral-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=six-box manduca_bilateral iter-4 (EXPLORATORY). (a) PRIOR FLAT: iter-1 (proj_sr=1.5) hr=0.05982; iter-2 (proj_sr=3.0) hr=0.05978; iter-3 (bf_d_w_ratio 1/6->0.5 i.e. proj spatial sigma 0.83px->2.5px, AND proj range wide) hr=0.05983. So EVERY proj-domain bilateral lever (range bandwidth proj_sr, spatial footprint bf_d_w_ratio) is FLAT to <1e-4. (b) FAILURE MODE / WHY PROJ-BILATERAL IS FLAT: the truncation-corrected FBP is already a strong reconstruction; the ~7-param proj-domain bilateral acts on the SINOGRAM before backprojection, where its tiny correction is smeared across all detector channels and largely washed out by the ramp filter + backprojection averaging, contributing almost nothing to the final image-domain SSIM/headroom. The binding constraint is NOT projection-domain noise bandwidth - it is that no operator is yet touching the reconstructed IMAGE where SSIM/hr are actually measured (img_n_bf=1 is a single shallow image-bilateral pass). (c) LEVER (one knob): img_n_bf 1->2, stacking a second image-domain trainable bilateral filter directly on the reconstructed image. This is a genuinely DIFFERENT axis from the 3 flat proj-domain iters: it doubles the image-domain denoising capacity at the exact location where the calibrated-SSIM-headroom metric lives, so surviving soft-tissue noise in the FBP output gets a second edge-preserving smoothing pass - the most direct route to move SSIM/hr. (d) BUDGET: +1 image-bilateral filter is ~7 extra params and one extra cheap conv per forward pass -> wall stays ~387-563s as iter-1/2/3, comfortably inside the hard 20-min budget. (e) BASE_ITER=3 (hr-best @ 0.05983, marginally best; preserves the iter-3 proj spatial-sigma=2.5px state and layers the image-domain capacity on top)., bf_d_w_ratio=0.5, img_n_bf=2

BUDGET REASONING (the load-bearing decision): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. val=ALL 214 L277 slices is MANDATORY (protocol; do NOT reduce). 18-min outer wall (naf_outer_wall_s=1080, inside the 20-min compute budget, leaving headroom for the figure+IO before the 30-min sbatch kill) / 214 scenes = naf_per_scene_s=5.0 s/scene. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT -- solver_plan.md flags NAF/R2G hr~0 on dense-view; the discarded boundary-slice run hinted naf 0.911 < LD-FBP ~0.81-cal baseline, a behavior hint only) AND it is BUDGET-STARVED on the 214-slice protocol (5 s/scene = far too few per-scene Adam steps for a NeRF-style convergence). Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the LD-FBP baseline (hr near 0). This iter ESTABLISHES that datapoint under the corrected metric -- a real finding (do NOT reduce val_n below 214 to make NAF look better). iter-2+ will tune ONE knob (per-scene step budget vs MLP capacity vs lr) but NAF cannot escape its structural ceiling on this dense substrate within a 20-min/214-scene budget.

advice_for_others: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=4, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.01, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (search-20260619-01, naf). SIX-BOX. (1) iter-1 NUMBERS: SSIM 0.4729, hr 0.0, PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08; elapsed 1097s; naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_hidden=128, naf_layers=4, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2; SLURM [fit] log shows each scene fit only ~85-97 Adam steps (median 91) before the 5.0s per-scene wall, and the 18-min outer wall (1080s) was hit EXACTLY at scene 214 (elapsed 1082.5s). (2) FAILURE MODE: budget-starved per-scene INR fit. A NeRF-style coordinate-MLP wants hundreds-to-thousands of Adam steps to leave its water-mu init; ~91 steps/scene leaves the MLP barely moved -> SSIM 0.4729 well below the LD-FBP baseline. This is starvation, NOT (yet) the structural floor. (3) ONE KNOB: naf_hidden 128->64 (naf_layers=4, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, val_n=214 ALL UNCHANGED). 214-SCENE 20-MIN BUDGET MATH (measured): the entire budget is the per-scene fit loop (train_n=0); total = 214 x per_scene_s = 214 x 5.0s = 1070s ~= the 1080s/18-min outer wall, hit exactly at scene 214. I CANNOT raise per_scene_s (214 x wall is already full inside the 20-min compute budget). So to buy MORE Adam steps per scene at FIXED total budget I make each step CHEAPER: per-step cost ~0.055 s/step is the fixed 2304-view fan-beam forward+backward PLUS the tunable 512^2-coord MLP forward; halving width 128->64 cuts the dominant hidden x hidden matmuls ~4x, so each 5.0s scene should fit meaningfully more steps -> more useful optimization per scene within the SAME 214 x 1080s/18-min wall. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I shrink naf_hidden 128->64, I expect SSIM to rise above 0.4729 because the cheaper MLP buys more Adam steps per scene, letting the INR move further off its water-mu init within the same per-scene wall. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.47 despite more steps, NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT), not merely starved. (5) HARD 20-min budget: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18 min) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall = the governor; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap), val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

advice_for_others: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_encoding=hash, naf_hash_levels=16, naf_hash_feat_dim=2, naf_hash_log2_size=19, naf_hash_base_res=16, naf_hash_max_res=512, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=32, naf_layers=3, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.02, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-6 (search-20260619-01, naf). PAPER-FIDELITY AUDIT FIX (A): add the Instant-NGP multi-resolution HASH encoding (config-gated, user-authorized 2026-06-20). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) NUMBERS trajectory (Fourier-PosEnc path, all hr=0, monotone climb via leanness+lr then a regression): iter-1 hidden=128,layers=4,lr=1e-2 -> SSIM 0.4729 (PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08, ~91 Adam steps/scene at the 5.0s per-scene wall). iter-2 hidden 128->64 -> 0.4943 (+0.0215). iter-3 layers 4->3 -> 0.5452 (+0.0509). iter-4 lr 1e-2->2e-2 -> 0.5629 (PSNR 20.28, RMSE 0.004843) = BEST. iter-5 lr 2e-2->4e-2 -> 0.3592 REGRESSED (lr lever exhausted, short-Adam instability). So iter-6 REVERTS to the iter-4 BEST scalars (hidden 64->32 SMALL MLP per the reference, layers 3, lr 2e-2) and changes the ARCHITECTURE: naf_encoding fourier->hash. (2) FAILURE MODE the fix targets: the Fourier-PosEnc -> vanilla-MLP path is the WRONG inductive bias and is budget-starved (~90-100 steps/scene leaves the coordinate-MLP barely off its water-mu init). The NAF paper's headline contribution is a multi-resolution HASH grid (Instant-NGP) feeding a SMALL MLP -- that is what makes it converge in few steps. The shipped solver had only a plain Fourier PosEnc (audit gap A). (3) ONE KNOB (architecture, user-authorized code fix): naf_encoding 'fourier'->'hash'. New pure-torch HashEncoding: 16 levels, feat_dim 2, log2_hashmap_size 19, base_res 16 -> max_res 512 (geometric: [16,20,25,32,40,51,64,81,102,128,161,203,256,323,406,512]), standard spatial hash h=(ix*1)^(iy*2654435761) mod 2^19, bilinear interp per level, concat -> 32-dim feature -> SMALL MLP (naf_hidden 64->32, naf_layers 3). All other knobs reverted to iter-4 BEST (lr 2e-2, n_freqs 8 unused on the hash path, tv 1e-4, n_clip 0.05). LOCAL+CLUSTER VALIDATION before dispatch: py_compile clean both sides (sha match), and a direct-fit smoke (structured disk-on-bg target) shows the hash path drops loss 99.1% in 60 steps with healthy table gradients (9.1e-5) vs the Fourier path 97.5% -- the hash encoder learns and converges slightly FASTER per step, confirming the code path is correct + the tables are in the autograd graph. (4) HYPOTHESIS: the hash grid's locality + multi-resolution structure converges faster off init than the Fourier MLP in the SAME ~90-100 steps/scene, so SSIM rises above the 0.5629 iter-4 Fourier best. HONEST EXPECTATION (audit): even a FAITHFUL hash-NAF is REGIME-BOUNDED on DENSE 2304-view Mayo (LD-FBP near-complete -> hr likely stays ~0); the hash encoding's real payoff is convergence speed/SSIM here and the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks elsewhere. FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= ~0.56 despite the faithful hash encoder, the per-scene-INR fit is structurally bounded on dense Mayo (document the hash-NAF ceiling as a NEGATIVE result, fix validated as runs+no-regress). (5) HARD 20-min budget UNCHANGED: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18-min in-solver outer wall = governor) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap so the WALL governs). 214x5.0s=1070s ~= 1080s outer wall (hit ~scene 214 every iter; well inside the 30-min sbatch kill). The hash MLP is SMALLER (32 vs 64 hidden) but adds a 16-table gather/step; per-step cost stays dominated by the fixed 2304-view fan-beam forward+backward, so the step count per 5.0s scene is comparable. val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (inlined single-val-ps probe -> L277 native ps ~0.73979), bg_target=truth, 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

FAILURE MODE: hr 0.2378 still far below ITNet v1 (0.4398); at 2798p the single-scale 3-layer CNNReg has eff RF only ~7px, too small for Mayos correlated streak/low-dose noise (~15-20px). So the lever is FLAT (single-scale, NO pooling) capacity + larger RF. CHANGE (CODE, ONE genuine change - the regulariser module): REWROTE CNNReg into a FLAT DILATED residual CNN. Keep reg_type cnn but GROW it: cnn_channels 12->32, cnn_layers 3->5, add per-layer DILATION ladder cnn_dilations=[1,2,4,2,1] (reflect-padded per dilation so spatial size preserved) -> eff RF expands ~7px->~21px at FULL resolution with ZERO downsampling. 37601 reg params (37602 total incl 1 scalar alpha), verified locally: size-preserving on 321px, reg(x)=0 at init (zero-init 1x1 head), iter-4 baseline reproduces 2797 exactly. ~6x SMALLER than ITNet 233k, within ~10-80k target. HYPOTHESIS: flat dilated capacity supplies the long-range context where POOLED capacity FAILED (iter-2/iter-5 capped psnr 32.4); staying full-resolution never blurs/aliases the recon the way pool->upsample does, so it should lift hr ABOVE iter-4 0.2378 toward 0.44 - the exact failure mode iter-5 could not. CLEAN A/B vs iter-5: same trainer, similar ~26-38k capacity, ONLY difference flat-dilated (no pooling) vs multi-scale (pooling). WHY STABLE (not iter-3): recon DYNAMICS unchanged (same K=5, single scalar alpha, plain prox step, cosine LR only DECREASES step from known-stable iter-4 lr); only the reg internal width/depth/dilation grows; zero-init head keeps reg(x)~0 at init so seed = iter-4 GD+DC. BUDGET: dilated convs same FLOP as dense; per-step cost DOMINATED by unchanged DC term (fwd+back project); extra conv width/depth small fraction; max_train_s=1080 hard backstop. PREDICTED hr ~0.28-0.34., reg_type=cnn, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, per_step_alpha=False, momentum=False, cnn_channels=32, cnn_layers=5, alpha_init=0.1, clip_max=0.05, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, cosine_lr_min=1e-05, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, cnn_dilations=[1, 2, 4, 2, 1]

advice_for_others: param_efficient-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=iter-10 SIX-BOX (NEW ARCHITECTURE STAGE: learned-init refiner of the LD-FBP). PREV CHAMPION iter-7 (foe nf24/k7/nb31, 1921p, K=5 tied prox+DC, scalar alpha, 16-ep cosine) hr 0.2515 ssim 0.906 psnr 36.59. DEAD LEVERS: iter-8 SCALED the FoE bank nf24->40 and TOTALLY DIVERGED (psnr 1.87); iter-9 DEEPENED the unroll K5->7 and DIVERGED (psnr 11.38). Both capacity AND depth blow up in 20 min: iter-7 is a SHARP, NARROW stable optimum (K=5, 1921p, 16-ep). FAILURE MODE: with reg-capacity and unroll-depth both exhausted, attack the part that is NEITHER: the INITIALISATION. iter-7 starts the unroll from the raw LD-FBP (psnr ~34.08 floor); the headroom GATE is RMSE-vs-LD-FBP and the unroll is a contraction, so a LOWER-RMSE x_0 maps to a LOWER final RMSE. CHANGE (CODE, +89 params, K=5 KEPT, a real two-stage architecture not a config tweak): ADD a tiny ZERO-INIT learned-init refiner g applied ONCE to the LD-FBP before the unroll: x_0 = clamp(LD-FBP + g(LD-FBP), 0, clip_max). g = 1->8 3x3 conv, ReLU, zero-init 1x1 head (init_channels=8, init_layers=1 => 8*9+8 + 8+1 = 89p). Total = 1921 + 89 = 2010p (<2.2k, <233k ITNet). UNROLL UNCHANGED iter-7 byte-for-byte: reg_type=foe nf24/k7/nb31 (1920p zero-init rho), n_iter=5, single scalar alpha, NO momentum/per-step alpha, plain prox, cosine 5e-3->1e-5, 16 ep, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, bs=1, val_n=214. STABILITY (why it STAYS in the iter-7 basin, unlike iter-8/9): (1) ZERO-INIT head => g=0 at init so x_0==LD-FBP EXACTLY, the seed IS iter-7 byte-for-byte; training only learns a correction (same zero-init-output pattern as CNNReg head / FoE rho). (2) K STAYS 5 -- the unroll dynamics iter-9 destabilised are UNTOUCHED; g is OUTSIDE the loop, applied once, so it cannot interact with the per-step alpha that over-stepped at K=7. (3) the FoE bank STAYS 1920p -- the reg capacity iter-8 destabilised is UNTOUCHED. (4) g is single-scale (NO pooling, dodging iter-2/5 failure), eff RF ~3px -- the smallest learned-init, a local FBP-noise/DC refiner. (5) BUDGET preserved: g is ONE cheap conv pass per forward (NOT per step); per-forward cost is dominated by the 5 DC project pairs, so the 16-ep cosine that fit iter-7 in 1331 s still fits, max_train_s=1080 backstop. HYPOTHESIS: refining x_0 with a tiny zero-init learned filter lowers the RMSE the K=5 contraction starts from -> lower final RMSE (the headroom gate) -> hr ABOVE 0.2515 at +89p, SAME K=5/1921p-unroll. A MATCH ~0.25 maps init-saturation (the unroll drives the init to its fixed point regardless of x_0); a REGRESSION means the refiner learned a destructive correction despite zero-init (diagnosable, revert). PREDICTED hr ~0.25-0.30., reg_type=foe, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, per_step_alpha=False, momentum=False, cnn_channels=12, cnn_layers=3, alpha_init=0.1, clip_max=0.05, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, cosine_lr_min=1e-05, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, foe_rbf_init_std=0.0, foe_filter_init_std=0.05, foe_x_range=1.0, learned_init=True, init_channels=8, init_layers=1

advice_for_others: param_efficient-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=param_efficient-claude-agentic iter-11 SIX-BOX (FIX the iter-10 learned-init WIRING BUG). PREV RESULT iter-10 (learned-init refiner): hr 0, ssim 0.2923, psnr 11.38, RMSE 0.01349 (18x iter-7's 0.00074), 2010p. FROZE: epoch-1 train loss 1.9e-4 = exactly 100x iter-7's epoch-1 (3.4e-6), then flat 8 epochs, alpha barely moved, output degenerate. CHAMPION iter-7 (foe nf24/k7/nb31, 1921p, K=5 tied prox+DC, scalar alpha, 16-ep cosine) hr 0.2515 ssim 0.906 psnr 36.59. FAILURE MODE (a WIRING BUG, NOT a science result): the iter-10 head was correctly zero-init (g(.)=0 at init), BUT forward CLAMPED the raw LD-FBP to [0,clip_max] BEFORE the unroll: x_0=clamp(LD-FBP+g(LD-FBP),0,clip_max). clip_max==display_max==0.05; the LD-FBP has bright pixels (bone/contrast/spine mu>0.05) and iter-7 NEVER clamps its init (starts x=u0 RAW). So the init clamp TRUNCATED the LD-FBP -> x_0 was NOT byte-for-byte iter-7 (numerically verified: ||x0-u0||/||u0||=6.8e-2 from the clamp alone) -> unroll started from a corrupted high-RMSE init (100x epoch-1 loss) and never recovered. The learned-init HYPOTHESIS was never tested, only a broken build. CHANGE (CODE, +177 params, K=5 KEPT): re-wire the learned-init CORRECTLY. (1) TRUE byte-for-byte init: x_0=u0+g(u0) with NO upper clamp (clamp_min(0) only, a no-op since LD-FBP>=0); the unroll's per-step clamp handles range, exactly like iter-7's x=u0. So at init (g=0) x_0==LD-FBP EXACTLY. (2) SMOOTH refiner (avoids the dead-ReLU-before-zero-head trap): conv(1->16,3x3)->GELU->conv(16->1,1x1) with BOTH the 1x1 head weight AND bias zero-init (verified nn.init.zeros_ on each). 16*9+16 + 16+1 = 177p; total=1921+177=2098p (<233k ITNet). advice_for_others: param_efficient-claude-agentic: val_n=214, rationale=RECOMBINATION(b) at 0.09 — add an IMAGE-DOMAIN ORIENTED ANISOTROPIC term for RESIDUAL DIRECTIONAL streaks on top of the iter-28 champion (FoE+gentle Manduca PROJECTION filter, val hr 0.3942 @ 1,926p). [1 PRIOR] iter-28 (FoE+Manduca, 0.3942) is the 0.09 champion; iter-30 (FoE+Manduca+ISOTROPIC image bilateral) REGRESSED to 0.3812 — the isotropic image bilateral is REDUNDANT on the projection-domain streak fix (no gain). [2 FAILURE MODE] iter-30 showed an ISOTROPIC image prior cannot catch what Manduca leaves; but LD-CT streaks are DIRECTIONAL (photon-starved high-attenuation rays backproject as oriented streaks) and the gentle Manduca filter must stay soft (view-consistency) so it deliberately leaves residual directional streaks. An isotropic filter is the wrong tool for an oriented artifact. [3 ONE KNOB] add a config-gated ZERO-INIT-gain oriented anisotropic-smoothing residual ON TOP of FoE+Manduca: reg(x)=FoE(x)+gain*Sum_theta(x-G_theta(x)), G_theta = oriented anisotropic Gaussian (elongated ALONG theta sigma_along=2.0px, narrow ACROSS sigma_across=0.6px) at M=4 FIXED orientations {0,45,90,135}deg; analytic kernels (NO trainable conv weights), 2 shared learnable sigmas + 1 ZERO-INIT shared gain = +3 params (NOT a steerable/equivariant FoE reparam — that DIVERGED iter-24). Total 1,929p. Everything else iter-26/iter-7 byte-for-byte (K=5 tied prox+DC, single alpha, no momentum/per-step-alpha, peak lr 5e-3, partial cosine T_max=16, max_train_s=1080, train_n=200, val_n=214, mu>=0 only NO upper clamp, Manduca proj_filter_on=true). ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 150->400 (per-scene Adam steps; all other knobs held at iter-1). FAILURE MODE iter-1: SSIM 0.7383 < LD-FBP baseline 0.808 (hr=0), AND budget-starved -- the 1080s in-solver wall was HIT at sample 26/214 (log 765216: 42.4 s/scene = 282.9 ms/Adam-step, dominated by the dense 512^2 Gaussian rasterization + one 2304-view forward/backward proj). So iter-1 was BOTH under-fit per-scene AND covered only 12% of the 214 slices. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the 0.7383 is per-scene UNDER-FIT, not a structural ceiling -- 2.67x more Adam steps will lift per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738 (the discarded 20260614 run reached SSIM 0.89-0.92 at gs_n_iter=6000 on val_n=20). FALSIFIER: if the ~9 scenes that finish at gs_n_iter=400 score <=0.76 SSIM (no material lift over 0.738), under-fit is REFUTED and 0.738 is a per-scene structural ceiling. BUDGET MATH: 282.9 ms/step x 400 steps = 113.2 s/scene; 1080s outer wall / 113.2 = ~9/214 scenes finish (well within the 20-min train+score budget; SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced); the per-scene loop self-truncates at the 1080s wall and scores whatever completed -- exactly as iter-1. This documents the R2Gaussian-lite quality-vs-coverage tradeoff on the 214-slice Mayo protocol: 6000 iters -> 0 scenes, 400 -> ~9, 150 -> 26 (none cover all 214 AND fit well -> structurally incompatible with the protocol, a real finding).

ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 400->60 (per-scene Adam steps DOWN to MAXIMIZE completed-scene COVERAGE; all other knobs held at iter-2). FAILURE MODE (the core, structural problem): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at a hard 20-min wall. Measured per-scene step cost is a clean linear function of gs_n_iter: iter-1 (n_iter=150) = 42.45 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 26/214 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335, hr=0; iter-2 (n_iter=400) = 113.0 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 10/214 (4.7% coverage), SSIM 0.736981, hr=0. Linear fit: 0.2822 s/Adam-step (offset ~0). iter-2 FALSIFIER FIRED: the hypothesis 'more Adam steps lifts per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738' is REFUTED -- 2.67x more steps (150->400) moved the average-over-214 SSIM by -0.0001 (0.7383 -> 0.7370, FLAT). So per-scene quality is NOT the lever; the average is dominated by the ~95% of scenes that NEVER complete (scored at/near their FBP init). DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION for iter-3: does COVERAGE win? At gs_n_iter=60 -> per-scene = 0.2822*60 = 16.9 s -> 1080s outer wall / 16.9 = ~64/214 scenes complete (30% coverage, ~2.5x iter-1's 26, ~6.4x iter-2's 10). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): if the average-over-214 SSIM goes UP at 64-scene coverage (vs 0.738 @ 26 scenes and 0.737 @ 10 scenes), coverage is the lever and R2-Gaussian is coverage-limited (not quality-limited) on Mayo. FALSIFIER: if average-over-214 SSIM stays ~0.74 or WORSE even at 2.5x coverage, then BOTH levers (per-scene quality AND coverage) are exhausted within the 20-min budget -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol -> file the quality-vs-coverage tradeoff as a documented NEGATIVE RESULT (no gs_n_iter both covers all 214 AND fits per-scene: covering all 214 in 1080s needs n_iter<=18 steps, which is a non-recon). BUDGET MATH: 64 scenes * 16.9 s = 1082s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/iter-2); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (26/214) -> iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-3 predicted ~0.74-0.76 if coverage helps (64/214), or ~0.74 (structural negative) if it does not.

LIMITER: r2gaussian is REGIME-BOUNDED on dense 2304-view Mayo — LD-FBP (~0.808) is near-complete, the inverse is not ill-posed enough for a Gaussian-splat prior to add value, so hr>0 is implausible regardless. Secondary (now FIXED) limiter was cold uniform random-init + pure-L2 loss; iters 1-5 (cold init, L2-only) all landed BELOW the 0.808 FBP init (SSIM 0.68-0.74, hr=0). iter-6 enabled the audit-fix (b) — FBP warm-start (gs_init_from_fbp=True: positions sampled prop to fbp^2, amp seeded from FBP intensity) + SSIM loss term (gs_ssim_weight=0.1; the benchmark is SSIM-scored but the loss was pure L2) — and lifted SSIM 0.7383->0.7519 (NEW run-best, +0.0136), hr still 0. TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) = the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) REGRESSED (lambda-up exhausted); iter-4 SSIM 0.926664 hr 0.208547 RMSE 7.825e-4 (tv_iterations 120->160, 1227.4s). So tv_iterations 160->200 is INFEASIBLE (cost model fit on the real iter-2/iter-4 pair: c_step=7.47 s/TV-iter, overhead=31.8s => n=200 lands ~1526s = ~25 min, a ~27% overshoot of the wall -> the 214-slice val pass would be killed / the metric invalidated) AND wrong-headed (the iterations lever is already flattening AND budget-capped). FAILURE MODE OBSERVED: the iterations lever has plateaued (120->160 gave +0.003 hr for +33% compute that blew the wall) -- the recon is NOT meaningfully iterations-limited at the cost the budget allows. iter-4's OWN falsifier named the next probe: 'tv_lr (finer convergence per step)'. HYPOTHESIS: doubling the step size (tv_lr 0.01->0.02) lets each of the budget-safe 120 gradient-descent steps travel ~2x further down the data-term gradient, so the recon reaches a LOWER data-term residual within 120 steps (the same/lower residual the 160-iter run was crawling toward) at ZERO extra compute, lowering val_rmse below 7.825e-4 so hr rises above iter-4's 0.208547 -- the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual. Why lr is the right convergence lever and not more iters: the GD schedule is step = lr/(1+decay*it), so with decay=0.01 the per-step distance shrinks ~2.4x by it=119; raising base lr counteracts that decay and converges the data term in fewer steps -- the budget-free way to test the convergence-vs-ceiling question the iter-4 falsifier left open. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.208547 (no gain, or a regression from GD overshoot/oscillation at the larger step), then (a) if hr drops sharply the step is too big and GD overshoots the TV-regularized minimum, and (b) if hr is merely flat then TV is at its REGULARIZATION CEILING on real Mayo LDCT (~0.924 SSIM / ~0.21 hr): 120 iters at lr=0.01 was already converged, the +0.003 from 160 iters was just residual noise, and BOTH the iterations lever (plateaued + budget-capped) AND the step-size lever are exhausted -- accept ~0.21 hr as the structural classical-TV ceiling on this real LDCT substrate and STOP tuning convergence knobs. BUDGET: tv_lr is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- tv_iterations stays at the budget-proven 120 -> identical ~928s wall (cost model: 31.8 + 120*7.47 = 928s, 77% of the 1200s budget, ~272s margin; even at +10% GPU-contention step-cost variance it lands ~1018s, still comfortably under the wall). This DELIBERATELY reverts the over-budget tv_iterations=160 back to 120: the 20-min budget is HARD with no exceptions (six-box rule 5), and iter-4 at 160 already breached it. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-1 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric): feasibility baseline, NO prior iter. Unrolled K=10 TV-GD with per-iter learnable step+lambda (20 trainable scalars), supervised-L2 vs clean truth, init from LD-FBP. SEEDED from the sibling classical tv_iterative iter-1 corner (SSIM 0.92298 / hr 0.133): tv_step_init=0.01 (=classical tv_lr), tv_lambda_init=0.001 (=classical tv_lambda), tv_clip_max=0.05. ADDS a SHORT supervised training phase (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1) on top of the 214-slice val pass. BUDGET (HARD 20 min train+score): classical tv_iterative ran 120 GD-iters x 214 slices in 918s (~0.036 s/slice-iter, dominated by the 2304-view 512px projector pair). This variant: val = K=10 unrolled x 214 slices, val_chunk=5 -> ~80-120s. Train = 40 samples x 8 epochs x K=10 x (fwd+bwd, ~2-3x a val slice-iter) ~ 256-380s. + 214-slice FBP precompute + load ~120s. Total ~7-10 min, ~2x margin under the 1200s wall. bs=1 holds only one K-step autograd graph at a time (memory-safe on 16 GB; no OOM risk vs the hammernik bs=4 OOM). FAILURE MODES TO AVOID: (a) 214-slice TV recon x training blows the wall -> kept K, train_n, epochs conservative; (b) under-training the 20 scalars -> epochs=8 gives the learnable step/lambda schedule room to depart from the seed while still fitting. HYPOTHESIS: a LEARNED per-iter lambda schedule lands at or slightly ABOVE the classical fixed-lambda tv_iterative hr 0.133, because the supervised end-to-end fit can adapt the data-vs-TV balance per unrolled step rather than holding one fixed lambda. If it under-performs the classical baseline, the K=10 unrolled depth (vs classical 120 iters) is the limiter and iter-2 raises tv_K.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). PRIOR: iter-1 SSIM 0.2855 / hr 0.0, elapsed 321.5s — FAR below the classical (non-trained) tv_iterative sibling (SSIM 0.92298 / hr 0.133). FAILURE MODE (diagnosed iter-1): tv_K=10 unrolled steps is FAR too shallow vs classical TV (~120 iters) -> the recon is severely under-resolved; the 20 learnable scalars cannot compensate for missing depth. ONE KNOB CHANGED: tv_K 10 -> 30 (3x deeper unroll). All else identical to iter-1 (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, lr=5e-3, val_n=214 ALL L277 slices, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00 with 10-min figure/IO headroom): iter-1 ran K=10 in 321.5s. Worst-case PURE-linear-in-K (assume all 321.5s is K-bound, fixed overhead=0): 32.15 s/K -> K=30 ~= 964s, ~20% under the 1200s wall. In reality a large slice of 321.5s is FIXED overhead (data load + 214-slice FBP precompute + per-ps probe ~60-120s), so the true K=30 cost is well under 964s. bs=1 holds only ONE K-step autograd graph at a time -> deeper K raises activation memory linearly but stays memory-safe on 16 GB (no OOM; cf. the hammernik bs=4 OOM). HYPOTHESIS: deeper unroll lifts SSIM toward the classical 0.92 band and clears baseline (hr>0), because 30 TV-GD steps resolve far more of the data-consistency + edge structure than 10 (closing the gap to classical 120 iters), and the learned per-iter step/lambda schedule adapts the balance across the deeper unroll. FALSIFIER: if SSIM/hr stay low at K=30, the limiter is NOT depth but the supervised-TV TRAINING (e.g. broken target/loss/optimisation), and iter-3 must check the training path (loss curve, learned step/lambda trajectory) rather than deepening further.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-05, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). RE-DIAGNOSIS from the iter-3 SLURM LOG (job 765340), which contradicts the iter-3 observation narrative: the 0.2855->0.8137 jump was NOT training un-freezing -- it is the LD-FBP PASSTHROUGH. Log facts: loss=0.000064 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs (did NOT decrease); lambda[k]=0.001 STILL PINNED at init for all 8 epochs (zero gradient); step[k] crept only 1.06e-8->1.76e-8. At tv_step_init=1e-8 the unrolled update f = f - step*(data_grad + lam*tv_grad) is scaled to ~zero, so the K=30 unroll is a near-identity map on fbp_init: pred ~= clamp(LD-FBP). That is why SSIM=0.8137 ~= the LD-FBP floor (~0.81), recon PSNR 33.60 is JUST BELOW baseline_PSNR 34.08, and hr=0.0 (the recon does not beat its own FBP). The freeze did not get fixed -- it MOVED: iter-1/2 (step=1e-2) froze via SATURATED-CLAMP (overshoot clamps the whole image, clamp derivative 0); iter-3 (step=1e-8) freezes via VANISHING-STEP (data+TV terms scaled to nothing, lam has no effect on the output so d loss/d lam ~= 0). FAILURE MODE (named): the limiter is the STEP SCALE, not depth (tv_K falsified iter-1->2) and not epochs/lr (lr=5e-2 already; scalars still don't move because the gradient to lambda is ~0 at both step extremes). The working step lives BETWEEN the two known-frozen regimes 1e-8 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-8 -> 1e-5 (the geometric midpoint sqrt(1e-8*1e-2)=1e-5 of the two frozen endpoints). At ~1e-5 the data-consistency term back_project(Rf-sino) actually moves the image OFF the FBP init across K=30 steps (so the recon depends on lambda -> non-zero gradient reaches log_lambda -> the 30 TV scalars can finally train), while staying INSIDE the [0,0.05] clamp basin (no whole-image saturation -> the clamp derivative is not 0 -> gradient also reaches log_step). Everything else IDENTICAL to iter-3 (lr=5e-2, K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-6, val_n=214 ALL L277, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0; tv_step_init STAYS finite/non-tiny -- do NOT revert toward 1e-8). HYPOTHESIS: with the step in the active basin, training un-freezes for REAL this time -- loss DECREASES across epochs, lambda[k] DEPARTS from 0.001 and step[k] adapts, and SSIM rises ABOVE the 0.8137 FBP passthrough toward the classical TV band (SSIM 0.85-0.92, the non-trained tv_iterative sibling hits 0.92 / hr 0.205); clearing hr>0 means the trained TV recon finally beats its own LD-FBP. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.81 with lambda STILL pinned (passthrough persists, the active basin is even narrower than 1e-5) OR collapses back toward ~0.286 (1e-5 already over-saturates the clamp), then the supervised-TV harness has NO step value that both trains the scalars AND beats FBP under Mayo's 2304-view unnormalized-adjoint scale within the config-only contract (the shared solver's raw back_project step is FORBIDDEN to edit) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is FBP-bounded on real Mayo LDCT) and STOP iterating this solver; iter-5 would only bracket the step further (e.g. 3e-6 / 3e-5) before declaring the negative. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score = 1200s wall): IDENTICAL compute to iter-3 (same K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, val_n=214, val_chunk=5 -- only the init VALUE of a scalar changes, not any loop size) -> ~918s measured iter-3, ~282s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 0.8137 (FBP passthrough, hr 0) -> iter-4 either >0.84 with lambda departing init and hr>0 (training un-froze for real) OR ~0.81 with lambda still pinned (passthrough -> bracket once at iter-5 then NEGATIVE RESULT + STOP).

BUDGET REASONING: the solver has NO in-code max_train_s wall hook (cannot add one -- must not edit the solver .py), so the budget is enforced by SIZING: with wu_n_outer=1 the per-sample cost is 1 band-weighted sparse-FBP (4-band backproject) + 1 forward_project + 1 dense-FBP + 1 back_project -- heavier than DD-UNet (iter-1 418s @ep8) but LIGHTER than the unrolled k=3 itnet_v3 (iter-1 738s @ep8) because there is no per-step unrolled DC loop; at only 6 epochs over 200 train slices the dominant cost is the 214-slice val pass at chunk=1 with the dense projector. This sizes train+score comfortably under the 20-min budget (30-min SLURM wall) with room for the figure. HYPOTHESIS: if I fit Wu-trainable at n_outer=1 / lr=1e-2 / ep=6 on 200 stratified Mayo train slices, I expect a finite val_ssim that lands in/near the LD-FBP baseline band (~0.84-0.89 SSIM, hr near 0), because Wu-trainable is a tuned-FBP family (band-reweighting + ONE soft-thresholded residual pass, NO image-domain CNN denoiser) and can only recover the small headroom that band weighting + a single residual correction buys over plain FBP -- it is structurally close to FBP, unlike the dual-domain U-Net families that landed hr~0.27. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR: iter-1 = SSIM 0.8370 / hr 0.0508, 8 params (wu_n_bands=4, wu_n_outer=1, ep6, lr0.01), elapsed 335s. iter-2 = SSIM 0.8390 / hr 0.0337, 8 params (SAME but ep18), elapsed 866.6s. iter-1->iter-2 (epochs 6->18) was FLAT: val_ssim +0.0020 (within the +-0.001 noise band the iter-2 falsifier set), and hr actually FELL 0.0508->0.0337. Per-epoch train cost = (866.6-335)/(18-6) = 44.3 s/ep at n_bands=4. SLURM log confirms training converged (loss=0.00000 by ep1; band_scale already saturating to clamp by ep18) -- epochs is INERT, the falsifier for under-training FIRED. (2) FAILURE MODE: few-param tuned-FBP ceiling. Wu-trainable is a band-reweighted aliasing-free FBP + ONE soft-thresholded dense residual pass with NO image-domain CNN denoiser; it sits hr~0.04 just above the LD-FBP floor and epochs cannot move it. The OPEN question iter-2's falsifier handed to iter-3: is hr capacity-limited (too few frequency bands to separate signal from noise) or is the whole FBP-family structurally ceilinged regardless of capacity? (3) ONE KNOB: CAPACITY via wu_n_bands 4->6 (+2 frequency bands in the band-weighted aliasing-free FBP, line 198 band-loop). This is the iter-2 falsifier's prescribed lever ('iter-3 must add capacity, wu_n_bands up'). I deliberately pick wu_n_bands over wu_n_outer because (a) n_bands enriches the FBP frequency partition -- the exact structurally-FBP part the ceiling hypothesis is about; (b) it is BUDGET-SAFE: the band-loop (FFT-filter + back_project) scales LINEARLY with n_bands while the heavy dense-projector residual pass stays a single fixed pass at n_outer=1, vs wu_n_outer++ which DOUBLES that dominant cost; (c) wu_n_outer=1 is the campaign 'mandatory' hint, leave it. NEW PARAM COUNT: wu_n_bands+2+2*wu_n_outer = 6+2+2*1 = 10 trainable scalars (was 8). epochs held at the iter-1 anchor 6 (NOT a second knob -- iter-2 PROVED ep6 vs ep18 is a non-difference, 0.837 vs 0.839; reverting to ep6 restores the proven-equivalent baseline epoch budget so the wider 6-band bank fits the HARD 20-min wall with margin, isolating n_bands as the sole meaningful change). All else identical to iter-1/2: lr0.01, bs=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214(ALL L277), grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, seed=42. FALSIFIER: if SSIM REGRESSES or stays FLAT (<=0.840, within noise of iter-1/2) at 6 bands, Wu-trainable is STRUCTURALLY FBP-ceilinged on Mayo regardless of capacity -- exactly matching the few-param-bilateral pattern THIS tick (dual_domain_bilateral_supervised img_n_bf 3->6: 0.9192->0.9057 REGRESSED; hammernik filters-up also regressed), i.e. capacity bumps DESTABILISE these few-param FBP-family denoisers rather than help. A regression would be the strong confirmation that the lever is the FBP family itself, not its band count. (5) HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score budget, sized via the ep6 anchor: worst-case (whole per-sample cost scaling with n_bands, which over-counts since the residual pass is fixed) ~1.5x the iter-1 per-epoch -> ~66 s/ep x 6 = ~396s train + ~120s for the 1.5x-wider 214-slice val pass ~= 520s, with the val FIGURE outside the budget and well under the 1800s SLURM kill. val = ALL 214 L277 slices (do NOT reduce); grad_clip=1.0; bs=1 + val_chunk=1 forced by per-sample-ps; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted; per-sample-ps FBP + per-sample model.proj/model.dense_proj swap; bg_target=truth; 321px detector-geometry FOV default (NO fov override).
